When an enumerated value is passed as an actual parameter, the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context that makes the enumerated value visible.
For a comparison operator, if the type of one of the operands is uniquely identified, it IS used as the type context for the other operand.
For the match operation, if the type of the value parameter is not identified, the type of the template parameter establishes the type context.
Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL only be reused within other structured type definitions.
Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL NOT be used for an identifier of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy.

An enumerated value MAY have a user-assigned integer expression or a non-empty list of integer literal values or ranges of integer literal values, given in parentheses after the name of the enumerated value.
A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL be statically bound and known at compilation time.
A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL evaluate to an integer value.
Each user-assigned integer value SHALL be distinct within a single enumerated type.
All ranges of all integer value lists of an enumerated type SHALL be disjoint.
A range in an integer value list of an enumerated type SHALL NOT include any of the single integer values used in that enumerated type.

An enumerated value without an assigned integer value IS associated with an integer number in the textual order of the enumerated values, starting at the left-hand side with zero, in steps of 1, skipping any number occupied by an enumerated value with a manually assigned value or value list.
The integer values associated with enumerated values ARE used to evaluate relational operators on enumerated values.
An enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL only be used as a value together with a specific integer value in parentheses after its name.
The integer value given in parentheses after an enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL be one of the values of that list.
An enumerated value with an associated integer value list MAY be used as a template of the enumerated type by adding a list of integer templates and ranges in parentheses after its name.
For an enumerated value with no assigned value or with a specific integer value assigned, the associated integer value SHALL NOT be used directly.

The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY be accessed using the predefined function `enum2int`, and an integer value MAY be converted into an enumerated value using the predefined function `int2enum`.
The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY also be used by the system to encode and decode enumerated values.

When a module parameter, formal parameter, constant, variable, non-parameterized template or parameterized template whose formal parameters all have default values is defined with an imported enumerated type, the name of that definition SHALL NOT be the same as any of the enumerated values of that type.
The TTCN-3 language IS defined to support the union type.
A union type IS a collection of alternatives, each identified by an identifier.
An actual union value IS a value in which exactly one of the specified union alternatives is present.
A union type IS suited to model data that can take one of a finite number of known types.
The value notation of a union value SHALL use the assignment notation.
The assignment notation for a union value SHALL assign a value to exactly one union alternative.
The union alternative assigned in the assignment notation of a union value IS the chosen alternative.
The not used symbol "-" SHALL NOT be used in a union value notation.
`omit` SHALL NOT be used in a union value notation.
The value list notation SHALL NOT be used for setting values of a union type.
A union alternative MAY be declared as the default alternative by using the `@default` modifier before the type of the alternative.
A union type SHALL NOT declare more than one union alternative as the default alternative.
If the union type has a default alternative, a union value IS compatible with the type of the default alternative according to the special type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.2.4.
If the default alternative of a union type is to be chosen, the assignment notation NEED NOT be used to denote a value of the union type.
If the default alternative of a union value is chosen, the default alternative selection (dot notation with the alternative identifier) NEED NOT be used to access the default alternative.
The list of effective fields of a union type IS defined to contain all alternative identifiers of the union type.

If a union type has a default alternative of a record type or set type, the list of effective fields of the union type IS defined to additionally contain all field identifiers of that record type or set type.
If a union type has a default alternative of a union type, the list of effective fields of the union type IS defined to additionally contain the list of effective fields of that union type.
A union type SHALL satisfy the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 in addition to the restrictions of clause 6.2.5.0.
All identifiers in the list of effective fields of a union type SHALL be distinct.
The default alternative of a union type SHALL NOT be of the anytype.
A union alternative SHALL be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId.

In a reference to a union alternative, TypeIdOrExpression SHALL resolve to the name of a union type or to an expression of a union type (e.g. a variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template or function invocation).
In a reference to a union alternative, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to the name of an alternative of the union type.
If the referenced value or template is of the anytype, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to a known type name or to a known type name qualified with a module name.
A union alternative SHALL NOT reference the union type definition it belongs to.

If a union alternative of a union type or of a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the type of the reference IS the set of values allowed by the constraints of the alternative declaration only, and constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored.
When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced alternative is not the chosen alternative, an error SHALL occur.
When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced union field or union value is omitted or uninitialized, an error SHALL occur.
When a union alternative is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative SHALL become the chosen alternative.
When a reference on the left hand side of an assignment contains alternatives of nested union values, all referenced alternatives SHALL become the chosen alternatives recursively.

When an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field, or of an omitted field (including a field omitted at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy), is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative.
When a value or value field of a union type is expanded, the union alternative referenced in the dot notation IS made the chosen alternative.

When expanding a left hand side reference to a union alternative, the expansion of record, record of, set, set of and array values and intermediate fields SHALL follow the rules of item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and of clause 6.2.2.1, correspondingly.
At the end of the expansion, the value of the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced union alternative.
The `optional` keyword SHALL NOT be used for a union alternative.
A union type definition MAY contain nested type definitions for the types of its union alternatives, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.3.
A union type definition MAY contain embedded fields, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.4.
The anytype IS a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.
If the address type is explicitly defined within a module, the anytype of that module SHALL include the address type as an alternative.
Each field name of the anytype SHALL be the name of the corresponding type, identifying the field uniquely.

An imported type whose name clashes with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module CANNOT be reached via the anytype of the importing module.
The anytype IS defined locally for each module.
An import statement SHALL NOT directly import the anytype of another module.
A user-defined type of the type anytype MAY be imported by another module.
Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype IS the means by which all types of the module where it is declared become accessible (as its alternatives) in the importing module.
A user-defined type of the type anytype IS a type containing all types imported into the module where it is declared.
A test suite writer SHOULD exercise due caution when importing a user-defined type of the type anytype into a module, as this may cause side effects.
An array IS a shorthand notation to specify a record of type.
An array MAY be specified at the point of a variable declaration, formal parameter declaration or function return value declaration.
An array MAY be declared as single-dimensional or multi-dimensional.
An array dimension SHALL be specified using a constant expression.
A constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL evaluate to a positive integer value.
A constant used in a constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
An array element IS accessed by means of the index notation ([]).
The index notation used to access an array element SHALL specify a valid index within the array's range.
An individual element of a multi-dimensional array CAN be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.
An array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.
Accessing an element outside the array's range SHALL cause a compile-time error or a test case error.
An array dimension MAY be specified using a range.
A range specifying an array dimension SHALL have inclusive boundaries only.
The lower and upper value of a range specifying an array dimension IS the lower and upper index value of that dimension, respectively.
The upper value of a range specifying an array dimension SHALL NOT be less than the corresponding lower value.
An array whose dimension is specified by a range IS equivalent to a record of type with a fixed length restriction of (upper bound - lower bound + 1), with indexing starting from the lower bound.
An array type with a variable number of elements CANNOT be defined.
An unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index CANNOT be defined.
The value of an array element SHALL be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.
Values of array elements MAY be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation, or several or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.
The value list notation and assignment notation for an array IS subject to the rules of clause 6.2.2.4.
The index notation MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
The index of the first element of an array SHALL be zero, or the lower bound of the index range if an index range has been given.
An array index SHALL NOT exceed the limitations given by the length or by the upper bound of the index range.
If the value of the array element indicated by the index on the right hand side of an assignment is undefined, an error SHALL be caused.
If the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, an error SHALL be caused.
Sending an array value with undefined elements SHALL cause an error.
An array element that is not set explicitly IS undefined.
When an element of an uninitialized array value or field or of an omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values of clause 6.2.2.4 SHALL apply.
When assigning a value to a multi-dimensional array, each dimension that is assigned SHALL resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.
In a value for a multi-dimensional array, the leftmost dimension IS the outermost structure of the value and the rightmost dimension IS the innermost structure.
An array slice of a multi-dimensional array MAY be used.
An array slice IS a reference to a multi-dimensional array value with fewer indexes than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition.
The indexes of an array slice SHALL correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right.
The indexes of an array slice SHALL conform to the related dimensions of the array definition.
An altstep MAY be activated as a default to capture recurring behaviour.
A default reference IS a unique reference to an activated default.
A test component SHALL generate a unique default reference when an altstep is activated as a default.
A default reference IS the result of an `activate` operation.
A default reference IS of the special predefined type `default`.
A variable of type `default` MAY be used to handle activated defaults in a test component.
The special value `null` IS an unspecific default reference.
The special value `null` MAY be used for the initialization of a variable of type `default`.
A default reference IS used in a `deactivate` operation to identify the default to be deactivated.
A default reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance in which the default was activated.
The actual data representation of the `default` type SHALL be resolved externally by the test system.
The TTCN-3 language IS NOT restricting the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of defaults.
A value of the `default` type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A port IS the means of communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface.
The TTCN-3 language IS supporting message-based ports and procedure-based ports.
A port type SHALL be defined as being either message-based or procedure-based.
A message-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `message`.
A procedure-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `procedure`.
A port IS bidirectional.
The communication direction of a port type list IS specified by the keyword `in` (in direction), `out` (out direction) or `inout` (both directions).
The operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` MAY be applied to a signature present in the in list of a procedure-based port.
The operations `call`, `getreply` and `catch` MAY be applied to a signature present in the out list of a procedure-based port.
The communication direction of a port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port.
The communication direction of a test system interface port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.

The in list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.
The out list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.
A port type definition SHALL have one or more lists indicating the allowed message types or signatures together with the allowed communication direction.
A port type MAY have one `map param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `map` operation.
A port type MAY have one `unmap param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `unmap` operation.
A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter.

If a signature is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the in direction of that port.

If a signature is defined in the in direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the out direction of that port.
A port used for communication with the SUT CAN need to address specific entities within the SUT.
The SUT CAN support several address schemes at different ports.
An address type MAY be bound to a port type.
A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be used for addressing purposes in communication operations.
A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be stored in a variable.

A message-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `message` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) MessageType list ";" entries, and "}".

A procedure-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `procedure` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) Signature list ";" entries, and "}".
A constant, variable or formal parameter MAY be of a port type.
A constant, variable or formal parameter of a port type CAN contain a reference to an existing component port or the special value `null`.
The special value `null` of a port type IS representing an unspecified port reference, i.e. the reference to no port.
A port type value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A port type SHALL have at most one address type bound to it.
A port type SHALL have at most one map parameter list defined.
A port type SHALL have at most one unmap parameter list defined.
A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter of a data type.
A MessageType in a message-based port type definition SHALL be a reference to a data type.
The term message IS used to mean both messages defined by templates and actual values resulting from expressions.
The list restricting what may be used on a message-based port IS a list of type names.
A component type IS defining which ports are associated with a component.
A port name in a component type definition IS local to that component type, and another component type MAY have ports with the same name.
All port names in the same component type definition SHALL be unique.
Unless stated otherwise, a component port IS having the same semantics as a constant of a port type.
A component type MAY contain declarations of constants, variables, templates and timers local to that component type.
The constants, variables, templates and timers declared in a component type ARE visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of that component type.
A testcase, function or altstep that uses the declarations of a component type SHALL explicitly state the component type in a `runs on` clause of its header.
A component type definition IS associated with the component instance and follows the scope rules of clause 5.2.
Each new instance of a component type IS having its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition, including any initial values.
A constant used in the constant expression of a type declaration for a component variable, constant or port SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
A constant used in the constant expression of an initial value for a component variable, constant, template or timer NEED NOT obey the restrictions of clause 10.
A component type definition has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".

A component type definition IS specifying the creation, declaration and initialization of ports, component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of the component type.
An instance of a component type MAY be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.
Every instance of a component type IS having its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.
A component instance IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A component type MAY declare port arrays, including multi-dimensional port arrays.
A component type MAY be defined as the extension of other component types using the `extends` keyword.

A component type extension has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier `extends` ComponentTypeIdentifier { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier } "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".
The component type defined with `extends` IS called the extended type.
A component type following the `extends` keyword IS called the supertype.
An extended component type IS implicitly containing all definitions from its supertype.
The definition of an extended component type including all definitions implicitly contained from its supertype IS called the effective type definition.
A component type MAY extend several supertypes in one definition, specified as a comma-separated list of component types.
A supertype of a component type extension MAY itself be defined by means of extension.

The effective component type definition of an extended type IS the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes, determined recursively, and the definitions declared directly in the extended type.
The effective component type definition SHALL be free of name clashes.
A definition contributed to the extended type by different supertypes via different extension paths IS NOT a different declaration and causes no error.
The semantics of a component type with extensions IS defined by replacing each component type definition with its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step before use.
A component reference of a component type CT1 that extends CT2 IS compatible with CT2, and testcases, functions and altsteps with `runs on` CT2 CAN be executed on it.
When defining a component type by extension, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and in the extended type.
A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between the supertype and the extended type.

When defining a component type by extending more than one supertype, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).
A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between different supertypes.
A component type defined by means of extension MAY itself be extended.
A component type extension SHALL NOT create a cyclic chain of definitions.
A component reference IS a unique reference to a test component created during the execution of a testcase.
A component reference IS syntactically one of `system`, `mtc`, `self` or an ObjectReference.
The test system SHALL generate a unique component reference at the time a test component is created.
The `create` operation IS returning the unique component reference of the created test component.
The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
The test system interface IS created automatically when testcase execution is started.
The `mtc` operation IS returning the component reference of the MTC.
The MTC IS created automatically when testcase execution is started.
The `self` operation IS returning the component reference of the test component in which `self` is called.
A component reference MAY be used in configuration operations such as `connect`, `map` and `start` to set up test configurations.
A component reference MAY be used for addressing in the `from`, `to` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface.
The special value `null` MAY be used to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. to initialize a variable of a component type.
The test system SHALL resolve the actual data representation of component references externally.
The TTCN-3 language IS NOT restricting the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of test components.
A component reference IS carrying the component type information of the referenced test component.
A variable for handling component references SHALL be declared with the corresponding component type name as its type.
A configuration operation SHALL NOT be applied directly to an array of component references.
When a configuration operation refers to a test component held in an array of component references, a specific element of the array SHALL be provided as the parameter of the operation.
The effect of an array of test components CAN be achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the result of a `create` operation to each relevant array element.
An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL be of a component type.
The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
An SUT CAN consist of several entities which can be addressed individually.
The global `address` type MAY be used for addressing SUT entities if only one address type is needed.

If several address types are needed at different ports for addressing SUT entities, the address type used for addressing via a port instance SHALL be declared in the corresponding port type definition.
An SUT address used for addressing IS syntactically a TemplateInstance.

The actual data representation of the address type IS resolved by an explicit global `address` type definition in the test suite, by address type declarations in port type definitions, or externally by the test system when `address` is left as an open type.

If an address type is bound to a port type definition, addressing of SUT entities in `to` and `from` directives of communication operations via instances of that port type SHALL be restricted to values of the bound address type.
If several address types exist within a test suite, ambiguities between them SHALL be resolved by means of the dot notation.
A reference to an address type in a variable definition used to store an SUT address MAY be prefixed by a port type identifier or a module identifier.

If both a global `address` type definition and port type definitions with an address declaration exist in a module, the global address type SHALL only apply to ports whose port type has no explicit address declaration.
A test suite SHOULD consistently use explicit address declarations in port type definitions rather than a global `address` type definition.
An explicit SUT address value of the global `address` type SHALL only be generated inside a TTCN-3 module if the `address` type is defined inside that module.

If the global `address` type is not defined inside the module, an explicit SUT address SHALL only be passed in as a parameter, received in a message field, or received as a parameter of a remote procedure call.
The special value `null` MAY be used as a value of the address type to indicate an undefined address, e.g. for initializing variables of the address type.

If a port type definition declares an address type, only values of that address type SHALL be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations of port instances of that port type mapped to the test system interface.
A TemplateInstance used for addressing SHALL be of type `address` or of the address type declared in the port type definition.
If a TemplateInstance used for addressing is of type `address`, it MAY be an address type value, an address type variable or another expression of the address type.
For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.
The address type SHALL NOT be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations of connected ports, i.e. ports used for communication among test components.
A structured type MAY be subtyped as given in table 3.
A value of a subtype SHALL fulfil the constraint of the subtype and all constraints of all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.
The number of elements of a value of a record of or set of type MAY be constrained.

A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS written as the `length` keyword followed by a single value or a range with inclusive boundaries in parentheses, placed between the `record` or `set` keyword and the `of` keyword.
A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS restricting the allowed number of elements of values of that type to the given value or range.
The value or the bounds of a length restriction of a record of or set of type SHALL be non-negative integer values, except for an upper bound given as `infinity`.
The `infinity` keyword MAY be used as the upper bound of a length restriction range of a record of or set of type.
If `infinity` is used as the upper bound of a length restriction, the maximum number of elements IS NOT constrained.
The upper bound of a length restriction range SHALL NOT be less than the lower bound.
A record of or set of type definition MAY be used as parent type to define a new record of or set of subtype.
When a new record of or set of subtype is defined from a referenced record of or set of type, the `length` keyword and the value or range SHALL be placed following the identifier of the new type.

The rules on the value and bounds of a length restriction (non-negative integers, `infinity` upper bound, upper bound not less than lower bound) SHALL also apply to length subtyping of referenced record of and set of types.
A constant used in a constant expression of length subtyping SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
List subtyping MAY be used when defining a new type based on an existing parent type.
List subtyping SHALL NOT be applied directly at the declaration of a core type.
A subtype defined by list subtyping IS restricting its allowed values to the values matched by at least one of the constraints in the list.
In list subtyping of record, set, record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and of arrays, the list MAY contain both subtypes and possibly partial templates of the core type.

Subtype references in a subtyping list SHALL be resolved recursively, so that the templates denoted by the referenced subtypes become members of an expanded list containing only possibly partial templates.
Every value present in the expanded list of a list subtype SHALL be a valid value of the parent type.
For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using value list notation SHALL be a complete template of the core type.
When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using assignment notation MAY be a partial template of the core type.

In a partial template defined with assignment notation in the expanded list of a record or set list subtype, a field that is not explicitly present SHALL be considered as containing AnyValue if it is mandatory and AnyValueOrNone if it is optional.
A TTCN-3 user SHOULD assign new values to single fields of values or templates of list-subtyped record or set types cautiously.

Assigning a new value to a single field of a value of a list-subtyped record or set type CAN cause an erroneous value when the new field value is not allowed in combination with the actual values of the other fields.
A list subtype of an enumerated type SHALL contain only values of the parent type.
A type restriction following the identifier of a newly defined record of or set of type (defined with the `record of` or `set of` keywords) SHALL constrain the innermost type.
The iterated type of a newly defined record of or set of type with a type restriction SHALL be a subset of the innermost type.
If the innermost type of a record of or set of type is a basic type, the subtyping rules of clause 6.1.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
If the innermost type of a record of or set of type references a structured type or anytype, the rules of clauses 6.2.13.1 and 6.2.13.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
A subtype definition of a structured type or anytype SHALL NOT mix different subtyping mechanisms (e.g. list and length subtyping).
Constants, variables and formal parameters of timer type MAY be defined.
A constant, variable or formal parameter of timer type CAN contain a reference to an existing timer or the special value `null`.
The special value `null` of timer type IS an unspecified timer reference.
The special value `null` MAY be assigned to a timer variable to explicitly reference no timer.
A timer reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance where the timer is defined.
A value of timer type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A map type IS a type that maps a set of unique keys to a set of values such that each key is associated with exactly one value.
Each key of a map type value IS associated with exactly one value.
A map type definition has the syntax `type map from` Type `to` Type Identifier.
The Type following the `from` keyword in a map type definition IS the key type of the map type.
The Type following the `to` keyword in a map type definition IS the value type of the map type.
A map value or template in index assignment notation has the syntax "{" ["*" ","] { "[" Index "]" ":=" Value "," } "}".
A map value MAY be denoted with the index assignment notation.
An index in the index assignment notation of a map value SHALL be a value of the key type of the map type.
The right hand side of an indexed assignment in the index assignment notation of a map value SHALL be a value of the value type of the map type.
A map template MAY use a mixed notation in which the first item is an asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments.
In the mixed notation of a map template, the asterisk representing AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be the first item.
When the index assignment notation is used on the right hand side of an assignment, each element to be changed IS identified explicitly by its key.
In the index assignment notation on the right hand side of an assignment, either a value or the not used symbol "-" MAY be assigned to an element identified by a key.
When the index assignment notation is assigned to a map variable, elements whose keys are not referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
Re-assigning a previously initialized element using the not used symbol or by skipping it in an assignment notation leaves that element unchanged.
In the index assignment notation, every index expression SHALL evaluate to a value different from all other index expressions of the same notation.
The unmap statement has the syntax `unmap` "(" ValueRef "," [SingleExpression | "*"] ")".
The `unmap` statement MAY be used to remove the mapping of a key to its associated value from a variable of a map type.
If the map variable does not associate the given key with a value, the `unmap` statement has no effect.
The `unmap` statement MAY be used to remove the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol from a map template variable.
When the `unmap` statement is used to remove AnyElementsOrNone from a map template variable, its second parameter SHALL be an asterisk literal.
If the map template variable does not contain the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, `unmap` with an asterisk as second parameter has no effect.
The ValueRef of an `unmap` statement SHALL be an initialized variable (or template variable) of a map type.
The SingleExpression of an `unmap` statement SHALL be a value compatible with the key type of the map type of the ValueRef.
The index notation on a map value or template has the syntax ValueRef "[" (Index | "*") "]".
The index notation on a map MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
The index notation with a key used on the right hand side refers to the value element that the map value or template associates with that key.
The index notation with an asterisk instead of an index used on the right hand side refers to the presence of the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol in the map template.
When the index notation with a key is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the value associated with that key is changed and values with other keys remain unchanged.
Assigning to the index notation with a key that already has an associated value causes the key to be mapped to the newly assigned value.
The presence of a mapping for a key MAY be checked by using the `isbound`, `isvalue` or `ispresent` operation with an index notation as its argument.
When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the presence of AnyElementsOrNone in the map template is changed and values and keys remain unchanged.
When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the left hand side of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment SHALL resolve into a boolean value.
When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the right hand side of an assignment, it returns a boolean value indicating whether AnyElementsOrNone is present in the map template.
The presence of AnyElementsOrNone in a map template MAY be checked by using the `isbound` or `ispresent` operation with an index notation containing the asterisk as its argument.
The index expression used in the index notation and in the index assignment notation of a map SHALL be completely initialized.
The index expression used in the index notation and in the index assignment notation of a map SHALL be compatible with the key (`from`) type of the map type.
When the index notation of a map value with a key is used as the left hand side of an assignment, the assigned value SHALL be compatible with the value (`to`) type of the map type.
The index notation used on the right hand side with a key that has no associated value SHALL result in a test case error.
The set of keys that a map associates with a value MAY be accessed using the `from` selector.
The `from` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `from`.
The `from` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `from`.
If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type `set of` A that contains all key values of MapValue.
The type `set of` A of the key set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.from.
In a map value, exactly one value IS mapped to each key.
Each value in the set of keys of a map value IS unique.
Comparing two elements with different indices of the set of keys of a map value using the equality operator IS always false.
The length of the set of keys of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
The order in which the keys of a map type value are enumerated IS NOT specified.
The set of values that a map contains MAY be accessed using the `to` selector.
The `to` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `to`.
The `to` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `to`.
If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.to yields a result compatible with type `set of` B that contains all values of MapValue.
The type `set of` B of the value set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.to.
The set of values of a map value CAN contain duplicate values, because two different keys can be mapped to the same value.
The set of values of a map value IS composed of exactly one value for each key value pair in the map.
The length of the set of values of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
The order in which the values of a map type value are enumerated IS NOT specified.

When an element of an uninitialized or omitted map value or field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
When a value or value field of map type is expanded, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.

During expansion of a map reference, expansion of record, record of, set of, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
A map type MAY have a nested structured type as its value (`to`) type.
The value (`to`) type of a map type MAY be a record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map type.
The key type of a map type SHOULD be a basic type.
Using complex structured types as key type of a map type CAN have a negative impact on the speed of execution.
In a map value, each key and its associated value field IS mandatory.
The `omit` symbol SHALL NOT be assigned to a map key or to a map value field.
A key IS removed from a map by the `unmap` operation (not by assigning `omit`).
A key of a map template SHALL NOT contain matching symbols.
A value field associated with a key of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, including `omit`, `*` and `ifpresent`.
The open type IS represented by the keyword `any`.
A value of any type MAY be passed directly as an actual parameter to a formal parameter of the open type without explicitly specifying a type context.
The open type SHALL only be used as the type of a formal parameter of a predefined or external function.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in a type declaration.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in a variable declaration.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in a template declaration.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in a constant declaration.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in a module parameter declaration.
The open type SHALL NOT be used as the type of a formal parameter of a template, testcase, altstep, non-external function, map operation or unmap operation.
The open type SHALL NOT be used in the return clause of a function.
A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the type of the target or of the other operand.
Value "b" IS the actual value that is assigned, passed as parameter, etc., in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
Type "B" IS the type of value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
An `address` type and its derivatives ARE subject to the same type compatibility rules as a type with the same definition but a name different from `address`.

A value "b" of a simple basic type or basic string type IS compatible with type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" and value "b" does not violate the subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".
A value "b" of charstring type IS compatible with a universal charstring type "A" unless value "b" violates a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

A value "b" of universal charstring type IS compatible with a charstring type "A" if every character of value "b" has a corresponding character (the same control or graphical character with the same character code) in the charstring type and value "b" does not violate a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
In clause 6.3.2, value "b" IS the value to be assigned (e.g. passed as parameter) to an object of type "A".
An enumerated type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an enumerated type.

An enumerated value "b" of an enumerated type "B" IS compatible with an enumerated type "A" if the identifier of value "b" is also defined in type "A" and the integer value(s) associated with value "b" are associated with the same identifier in type "A".

A value "b" of record type "B" IS compatible with record type "A" if the number and the optionality of the fields in textual order of definition are identical, the types of corresponding fields are compatible, and the value of each present field of value "b" is compatible with the type of the corresponding field in type "A".

When a value "b" of a record type is assigned to an object of a compatible record type "A", the value of each field of value "b" IS assigned to the positionally corresponding field of the value of type "A".

A value "b" of a `record of` type or array type IS compatible with a `record of` type or array type "A" if the element types are compatible and value "b" does not violate any length subtyping of the `record of` type "A" or the dimensions of the array type "A".

When a value "b" of a `record of` or array type is assigned to an instance of type "A", the element values of value "b" SHALL be assigned sequentially to the instance of type "A", including undefined elements.
An array type IS compatible with another array type if their corresponding `record of` types are compatible.
A set type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a set type.
A `set of` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a `set of` type.
The compatibility rules for record types SHALL apply to set types.
The compatibility rules for `record of` types SHALL apply to `set of` types.
When determining type compatibility of set types, the textual order of the fields in the set type definition IS decisive, although the order of elements at sending and receipt is unknown.
The arbitrary order of fields in a set value IS NOT relevant for type compatibility, because the field names identify which fields of the set type correspond to which set value fields.

A union value "b" of union type "B" IS compatible with union type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" has a corresponding alternative with identical name in type "A" and the value of the selected alternative is compatible with the type of that corresponding alternative.

A union value "b" of union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" IS compatible with an arbitrary type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is the default alternative and the value of the default alternative is compatible with type "A".
A value "a" of an arbitrary type "A" IS compatible with a union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" if value "a" is compatible with type "C".
When checking the compatibility of two union types, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL first apply the rule based on identically named alternatives, which does not depend on a default alternative.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use the default-alternative compatibility rules only if the rule based on identically named alternatives has not determined compatibility.
The prescribed order of the union compatibility rules IS intended to avoid ambiguity when a default alternative would also be compatible with the union type itself.
A union type with a default alternative CAN be nested within another union type with a default alternative.

Type compatibility along default alternatives IS transitive: the outermost union type is compatible with the type of the innermost default alternative if all containing alternatives are default alternatives.
A union value with a default alternative used in an expression IS resolved to its long notation (the default alternative) before the expression is evaluated.
A union value with a default alternative used directly in a `log` statement IS NOT converted to its default alternative; the union value itself is logged.
An `anytype` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an `anytype` type.
An `anytype` value "b" of `anytype` type "B" IS compatible with `anytype` type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is also contained in type "A".

Only an `anytype` type that is constrained to a fixed set of types via list subtyping CAN cause `anytype` incompatibility, namely when the set of types contained in type "A" does not contain the type selected in value "b".
The structured type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.2 ARE also valid for the sub-structures (fields and elements) of structured types.
A value of any TTCN-3 type IS compatible with an open type occurring on the left hand side of an assignment.
A value of an open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment IS compatible with type "A" if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with type "A".
A component reference "b" of component type "B" IS compatible with component type "A" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".

A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `runs on` clause MAY be called or started on a component instance of type "B" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".

A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `mtc` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has an `mtc` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B", if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
If the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running MTC, a runtime error CAN occur.

A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `system` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has a `system` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B" and no `system` clause, if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".

If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on, a runtime error CAN occur.
For component type compatibility, a port instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical port types and identical identifiers.
For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers.
For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL either both have identical initial durations or both have no initial duration.
For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers and identical types.

For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical initialization values; for variables, either both definitions have no initial value or both have the same value.

For component type compatibility, a component template in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers, types, formal parameter lists and assigned template or template field values.
The communication operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.
The connection operations `connect`, `map`, `disconnect` and `unmap` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.

The type of a value or template used directly as argument of a `send`, `receive` or `trigger` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.

The signature of the parameter list given to a `call`, `getcall`, `reply` or `getreply` operation, and the signature given to a `catch` or `raise` operation, SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.
The type of a value or template used directly as exception in a `catch` or `raise` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the exception list of the signature given to the operation.
A `receive` operation whose template is of a type "T" SHALL NOT match a message that was sent as a value or template of a different type, even if that type is a synonym of type "T".
Storing the value of a received message in a variable by a value redirect IS NOT subject to strong typing; the variable needs only be of a compatible type.
When a value has to be converted to a type with a different root type, the conversion SHALL use one of the predefined conversion functions of clause 16.1.2 or a user-defined function.
A reference to a port "b" of port type "B" IS compatible with port type "A" (for variables, constants and parameters of port types) only if type "B" and type "A" are equal or synonym types.
A timer reference IS compatible with any other timer reference (for variables, constants and parameters of timer types).
A map type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a map type.
A value "b" of map type "B" IS compatible with map type "A" if the from type of "A" is compatible with the from type of "B" and the to type of "B" is compatible with the to type of "A".

When a value of map type "B" is used in a variable of map type "A" whose from type is narrower, values associated with keys that are not values of the from type of "A" CANNOT be accessed through the variable.
A type MAY be defined as a synonym of another type.
A type synonym MAY be defined for every kind of type.
Synonym types ARE compatible with each other.
The automatic type MAY be used only in a variable declaration, a template variable declaration, a constant declaration or a module parameter declaration.
A variable, constant or module parameter declaration that uses the automatic type IS written without the type part.
The type of a declaration that uses the automatic type IS provided implicitly.
The automatic type IS equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment of the declaration.
The type of the expression or template body used for automatic typing SHALL be unambiguously determinable from the expression or template body itself.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing SHALL be one of the forms listed in items a) to q) of clause 6.5.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a reference to an existing variable, formal parameter, constant or template, or to a field or element inside of it.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a call of a function returning a value, including a predefined function.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a TTCN-3 operation returning a value, such as `match`, `valueof` or `ispresent`.

The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be an expression composed of several operands whose result type can be unambiguously resolved using the rules for expressions or automatic types.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a literal of the `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring` or `verdicttype` type.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a character string literal.
If a character string literal used for automatic typing contains only characters of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `charstring`.
If a character string literal used for automatic typing contains a character that is not of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `universal charstring`.
The template body used for automatic typing MAY be an inline template.
The expression used for automatic typing MAY be a qualified enumerated value.
A value list notation in which all values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `record of` the common type.
The common type of the values of a value list notation used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
An assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the assignment notation.
Each value in an assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
The name of each field of the automatic record type IS equal to the corresponding field name in the assignment notation.
The type of each field of the automatic record type IS the automatic type of the corresponding field value in the assignment notation.
A field of the automatic record type IS optional if the corresponding value in the assignment notation does not fulfil the requirements of the `present` template restriction.
A field of the automatic record type IS NOT optional if the corresponding value in the assignment notation fulfils the requirements of the `present` template restriction.
An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes are of the `integer` type and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `record of` the common type.
The common type of the item values of an index notation with integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.

An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes have a common type other than `integer` and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `map from` the common index type `to` the common value type.
The common type of the indexes and the common type of the item values of an index notation with non-integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
A template list with two or more items or a complemented template list, in which all templates have a common type, SHALL provide an automatic type equal to the common type.
The common type of the templates of a template list or complemented template list used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a value range.
The automatic type of a value range IS equal to the type of its bounds.
If both bounds of a value range used for automatic typing are infinity, the automatic type IS `integer`.
The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a pattern.
If a pattern used for automatic typing contains only characters or references of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `charstring`.
If a pattern used for automatic typing contains a character or reference that is not of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `universal charstring`.
A `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism in which all items have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `set of` the common type.
The common type of the items of a `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment, if its type context is unambiguous.
The template body of a declaration that uses the automatic type SHALL NOT consist only of the AnyValue matching symbol `?`, because `?` does not provide a type.
The TTCN-3 language IS a language that supports the specification of expressions.
An expression MAY be a template reference, a value reference or a literal without any operation involved.
An expression MAY be composed of the predefined operators defined in clause 7.1.
A template CAN be used at the right hand side of an assignment, in parameter passing and in (predefined) functions where template passing is explicitly allowed.

An expression IS either a SingleExpression, or a compound expression in assignment notation "{" { FieldReference ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) [","] } "}", or a compound expression in list notation "{" [ { ( Expression | "-" ) [","] } ] "}".
An expression MAY be built from other (simple) expressions.
A function used in an expression SHALL have a return clause.
An operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be a value.
The root type of an operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be one of the types specified for that operator in clauses 7.1.1 to 7.1.8.
An expression of a record, set, record of, set of, array, union or anytype type IS written in assignment notation or value list notation.
When an expression is evaluated, the evaluated value of an operand SHALL be completely initialized, unless the clause of the specific operator explicitly states otherwise.
The root type of an operand SHALL be one of the types specified for the operator applied to it.
The special value `null` SHALL NOT be used as an operand of an expression other than the equal (`==`) and not equal (`!=`) operators.
A field or element of a structured type that is referenced in an expression SHALL contain a completely initialized value.
A field or element of a structured type that is not used in an expression MAY be uninitialized or contain `omit`.
A predefined operator MAY be used in the terms of a TTCN-3 expression.
A predefined operator IS a member of one of the categories arithmetic, list, relational, logical, bitwise, shift, rotate or presence checking operators.
The arithmetic operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The list operator category IS a category of predefined operators.
The relational operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The logical operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The bitwise operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The shift operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The rotate operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
The presence checking operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
When an expression is evaluated, the evaluated value used as an operand of an operator SHALL be completely initialized, unless the operand is explicitly allowed to be partially initialized.
An operator listed in a row of table 6 IS of equal precedence to every other operator listed in the same row.
If more than one operator of equal precedence appears in an expression, each operation IS evaluated in left-to-right order.
Parentheses MAY be used to group operands in an expression.
A parenthesized expression IS of the highest precedence for evaluation.
The addition operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `+` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The subtraction operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `-` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The multiplication operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `*` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The division operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `/` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The modulo operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `mod` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The remainder operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `rem` and belongs to the arithmetic operators category.
The concatenation operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `&` and belongs to the string operators (list operator) category.
The equal operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `==` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The less than operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `<` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The greater than operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `>` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The not equal operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `!=` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The greater than or equal operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `>=` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The less than or equal operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `<=` and belongs to the relational operators category.
The logical not operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `not` and belongs to the logical operators category.
The logical and operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `and` and belongs to the logical operators category.
The logical or operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `or` and belongs to the logical operators category.
The logical xor operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `xor` and belongs to the logical operators category.
The bitwise not operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `not4b` and belongs to the bitwise operators category.
The bitwise and operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `and4b` and belongs to the bitwise operators category.
The bitwise or operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `or4b` and belongs to the bitwise operators category.
The bitwise xor operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `xor4b` and belongs to the bitwise operators category.
The shift left operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `<<` and belongs to the shift operators category.
The shift right operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `>>` and belongs to the shift operators category.
The rotate left operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `<@` and belongs to the rotate operators category.
The rotate right operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `@>` and belongs to the rotate operators category.
The field presence check operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `ispresent` and belongs to the presence checking operators category.
The chosen alternative check operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `ischosen` and belongs to the presence checking operators category.
The value check operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `isvalue` and belongs to the presence checking operators category.
The bound check operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `isbound` and belongs to the presence checking operators category.
The parentheses operator `( … )` IS of the highest precedence of all operators.
Each of the unary presence checking operators `ispresent`, `ischosen`, `isvalue` and `isbound` IS of higher precedence than the unary `+` and `-` operators.
Each of the unary `+` and `-` operators IS of higher precedence than the binary `*`, `/`, `mod` and `rem` operators.
Each of the binary `*`, `/`, `mod` and `rem` operators IS of higher precedence than the binary `+`, `-` and `&` operators.
Each of the binary `+`, `-` and `&` operators IS of higher precedence than the unary `not4b` operator.
Each of the unary `not4b` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `and4b` operator.
Each of the binary `and4b` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `xor4b` operator.
Each of the binary `xor4b` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `or4b` operator.
Each of the binary `or4b` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `<<`, `>>`, `<@` and `@>` operators.
Each of the binary `<<`, `>>`, `<@` and `@>` operators IS of higher precedence than the binary `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=` operators.
Each of the binary `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=` operators IS of higher precedence than the binary `==` and `!=` operators.
Each of the binary `==` and `!=` operators IS of higher precedence than the unary `not` operator.
Each of the unary `not` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `and` operator.
The binary `and` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `xor` operator.
The binary `xor` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `or` operator.
The binary `or` operator IS of the lowest precedence of all operators.

Dot notation, index notation and decoding notation (`=>`) SHOULD be evaluated from left to right, just after the parentheses operator and before the `ispresent`, `ischosen`, `isvalue` and `isbound` operators.
The expression `a.b[x].d=>e.f` IS equivalent to `((((a.b)[x]).d)=>e).f`, i.e. dot, index and decoding notations are evaluated left to right.
An arithmetic operator IS one of the operations addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, modulo and remainder.

An operand of an arithmetic operator SHALL be an integer value (including values of types derived from integer) or a float value (including values of types derived from float) containing a numeric value only.
An operand of the `mod` or `rem` operator SHALL be of type integer or of a type derived from integer.
The use of the special float values `infinity`, `-infinity` and `not_a_number` in arithmetic operators SHALL follow the rules defined in IEEE 754.
The result type of an arithmetic operation on integer operands IS integer.
The result type of an arithmetic operation on float operands IS float.
The operand of the unary `+` or unary `-` operator SHALL obey the same operand rules as the binary arithmetic operators (integer or numeric float value).
The result of the unary `-` operator IS the negated value of the operand (negative for a positive operand and positive for a negative operand).
The result of the unary `+` operator IS the value of the operand unchanged.
The result of the division operator `/` on two integer values IS the whole integer part of the quotient of the first integer by the second, with the fraction discarded.
The result of the division operator `/` on two numeric float values IS the float quotient of the first float by the second, without discarding fractions.
The result type of the `rem` and `mod` operators IS integer.
The result of `x rem y` and of `x mod y` IS the remainder of the integer division of x by y.
The right operand y of the `rem` or `mod` operator SHALL NOT be zero.
For positive x and y, `x rem y` IS equal to `x mod y`; for negative arguments the results differ.
`x rem y` IS defined as `x - y * (x/y)`.
When x >= 0, `x mod y` IS equal to `x rem |y|`.
When x < 0 and `x rem |y|` = 0, `x mod y` IS 0.
When x < 0 and `x rem |y|` < 0, `x mod y` IS `|y| + x rem |y|`.
For x = -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 the value of `x mod 3` IS 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0 respectively.
For x = -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 the value of `x rem 3` IS 0, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 0 respectively.
The list operator `&` IS the concatenation of values of string types, record of types, set of types or arrays.
The operands of the list operator `&` SHALL be of the same root type.
The list operator `&` IS a simple concatenation of its operands from left to right.
The list operator `&` IS NOT any form of arithmetic addition.
The result type of the list operator `&` IS the root type of its operands.
When the list operator `&` is applied to record of, set of or array values, both the outer type and the iterated inner type of the operands SHALL have the same root type, recursively.
Two or more value list notation expressions CAN be concatenated with `&` if the result is used as a record of or array of the same root type as the concatenated expressions.
When the list operator `&` is used for record of, set of or array values, its operands SHALL be at least partially initialized.
The relational operators ARE equality (==), less than (<), greater than (>), non-equality (!=), greater than or equal to (>=) and less than or equal to (<=).
The result type of a relational operator IS boolean.

An operand of the relational operators <, >, >= and <= SHALL be of type integer (including types derived from integer), of type float (including types derived from float), or an instance of the same enumerated type as the other operand.
The operands of a relational operator SHALL NOT be instances of different root types.
A value of the address type MAY be an operand of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators, independent of the actual type of the address type.
If the actual type of the address type differs from the types for which equality is defined, a value of the address type SHALL only be compared with the special value `null`.
An operand of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators SHALL be a completely initialized value or a field reference.
Except for enumerated types, the operands of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators SHALL be of compatible root types.
An instance of a type for which no equality rule is given in clause 7.1.3 SHALL NOT be an operand of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators.
Two field references ARE equal if both referenced fields are optional fields and both are set to `omit`.
Two field references ARE equal if both referenced fields, optional or not, are initialized with values and these values are equal.
A field reference IS equal to a value if the referenced field is initialized with a value and both values are equal.
Two integer values ARE equal if and only if they contain the same value.
Integer values ARE ordered by the normal mathematical ordering for the relational operators <, >, >= and <=.
Enumerated values of the same enumerated type or of different enumerated types MAY be compared.

An expression of enumerated type B SHALL only be compared with an expression of a different enumerated type A if A and B can be merged into a consistent larger enumerated type, i.e. no integer value is associated with different identifiers.
Two enumerated values ARE equal if and only if both their identifiers and their associated integer values, associated explicitly or implicitly, are the same.
Two float values ARE equal if and only if they contain the same value.
The float values minus zero and plus zero ARE two distinct values.
The float value minus zero IS less than plus zero, which represents zero.
Float values other than the special values ARE ordered by the normal mathematical ordering.
Each of the special float values -infinity, infinity and not_a_number IS equal only to itself.
The special value -infinity IS less than any other float value.
The special value infinity IS greater than any numerical float value and greater than -infinity.
The special value not_a_number IS greater than any other float value, including infinity.
Two charstring values, or two universal charstring values, ARE equal if and only if they have equal lengths and the characters at all positions are the same.
Two bitstring, two hexstring or two octetstring values ARE equal if and only if they have equal lengths and the bits, hexadecimal digits or octets, respectively, at all positions are the same.

Two record values, or two set values, ARE equal if and only if each is compatible with the type of the other operand, the actual values of all present fields are equal to their corresponding fields, and all fields corresponding to omitted fields are also omitted in the other value.

Two record of values, two set of values or two array values ARE equal if and only if each is compatible with the type of the other operand, both have the same length, and each element of one value is equal to the corresponding element of the other value.
A record of value and an array value MAY be compared; in this case the array is treated as a value of its corresponding record of type.

Values of the same union type, and values of different union types in which at least one alternative is compatible with the other type, MAY be compared, independent of whether a compatible alternative is the selected one.
Values of different union types in which no alternative is compatible with the other type SHALL NOT be compared.

Two union values ARE equal if and only if the names of the selected alternatives are identical, each value is compatible with the type of the other value, and the actual values of the selected alternatives are equal.
Values of the same anytype, or of the anytypes of any two modules, MAY be compared.
Two anytype values ARE equal according to the same rules as union values.
In the comparison of anytype values, user-defined types with the same name defined in different modules DO NOT denote the same selected alternative name.

Two default, two port, two timer or two component values ARE equal if and only if both are initialized with the special value `null` or both refer to the same default, port, timer or test component, independent of the actual state of that object.
A compound expression (assignment notation or value list notation) MAY be used directly as an operand of a comparison operation of a structured type.
If both operands of a comparison operator are compound expressions, both SHALL be value list notation expressions.
If both operands of a comparison operator are value list notation expressions, all their elements SHALL be of the same root type.
If both operands of a comparison operator are value list notation expressions, they ARE compared like record of values whose element type is the common root type of the elements.
If only one operand of a comparison operation is a compound expression, the compound expression SHALL be compatible with the root type of the other operand.
If only one operand of a comparison operation is a compound expression, the operands ARE compared like values of the root type of the other operand.

Two map values ARE equal if and only if each is compatible with the type of the other operand, they have the same number of key-value pairs, and for each key-value pair in either map the other map has a key-value pair with an equal key and an equal value.
The boolean operators ARE negation (`not`), logical and (`and`), logical or (`or`) and logical xor (`xor`).
An operand of a boolean operator SHALL be of root type boolean.
The result type of a boolean operator IS boolean.
The unary `not` operator returns `true` if its operand is `false` and returns `false` if its operand is `true`.
The `and` operator returns `true` if both operands are `true`, and `false` otherwise.
The `or` operator returns `true` if at least one operand is `true`, and `false` only if both operands are `false`.
The `xor` operator returns `true` if exactly one operand is `true`, and `false` if both operands are `false` or both are `true`.
The evaluation of the operands of a boolean operator IS stopped once the overall result is known (short circuit evaluation).
If the left operand of the `and` operator evaluates to `false`, the right operand IS NOT evaluated and the expression evaluates to `false`.
If the left operand of the `or` operator evaluates to `true`, the right operand IS NOT evaluated and the expression evaluates to `true`.
The bitwise operators ARE bitwise not, bitwise and, bitwise or and bitwise xor.
The bitwise not, and, or and xor operators ARE named `not4b`, `and4b`, `or4b` and `xor4b` respectively.
An operand of a bitwise operator SHALL be of root type bitstring, hexstring or octetstring.
The two operands of the `and4b`, `or4b` and `xor4b` operators SHALL be of the same root type.
