The result type of a bitwise operator SHALL be the root type of its operands.
The unary `not4b` operator inverts each bit of its operand: each 1 bit is set to 0 and each 0 bit is set to 1.
The two operands of the `and4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
For each bit position of the operands of the `and4b` operator, each result bit IS 1 if both corresponding operand bits are 1, and 0 otherwise.
The two operands of the `or4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
For each bit position of the operands of the `or4b` operator, each result bit IS 0 if both corresponding operand bits are 0, and 1 otherwise.
The two operands of the `xor4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
For each bit position of the operands of the `xor4b` operator, each result bit IS 0 if both corresponding operand bits are 0 or both are 1, and 1 otherwise.
The shift operators ARE shift left (<<) and shift right (>>).
The left-hand operand of a shift operator SHALL be of root type bitstring, hexstring or octetstring.
The right-hand operand of a shift operator SHALL be a non-negative integer.
The result type of a shift operator SHALL be the root type of the left-hand operand.
If the left-hand operand of a shift operator is of type bitstring, the shift unit IS 1 bit.
If the left-hand operand of a shift operator is of type hexstring, the shift unit IS 1 hexadecimal digit.
If the left-hand operand of a shift operator is of type octetstring, the shift unit IS 1 octet.
The shift left operator (<<) IS a binary operator with a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
The shift left operator (<<) shifts the left-hand operand to the left by the number of shift units given by the right-hand operand.
Shift units shifted out of the left-hand operand by the shift left operator (<<) ARE discarded.
For each shift unit shifted to the left, the shift left operator (<<) inserts a zero ('0'B, '0'H or '00'O, according to the type of the left-hand operand) at the right-hand side of the left operand.
The shift right operator (>>) IS a binary operator with a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
The shift right operator (>>) shifts the left-hand operand to the right by the number of shift units given by the right-hand operand.
Shift units shifted out of the left-hand operand by the shift right operator (>>) ARE discarded.
For each shift unit shifted to the right, the shift right operator (>>) inserts a zero ('0'B, '0'H or '00'O, according to the type of the left-hand operand) at the left-hand side of the left operand.
The predefined rotate operators ARE the rotate left operator `<@` and the rotate right operator `@>`.
The left-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL be of root type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of` or `set of`.
The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL be a non-negative integer value.
The result type of a rotate operator SHALL be the root type of its left-hand operand.
An array MAY be used as the left-hand operand of a rotate operator, because the root type of an array is `record of`.
The behaviour of a rotate operator IS determined by the type of its left-hand operand.
If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `bitstring`, the rotate unit applied IS 1 bit.
If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `hexstring`, the rotate unit applied IS 1 hexadecimal digit.
If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `octetstring`, the rotate unit applied IS 1 octet.
If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `charstring` or `universal charstring`, the rotate unit applied IS one character.
If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `record of`, `set of` or array, the rotate unit applied IS one element.
The rotate left operator `<@` IS a binary operator taking a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
The rotate left operator `<@` rotates the left-hand operand to the left by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
For the rotate left operator `<@`, the rotate units shifted out on the left IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.
When a rotate operator is applied to a `record of`, `set of` or array value, the left-hand operand SHALL be at least partially initialized.
The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL additionally satisfy restriction a) of clause 6.5.
The rotate right operator `@>` IS a binary operator taking a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
The rotate right operator `@>` rotates the left-hand operand to the right by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
For the rotate right operator `@>`, the rotate units shifted out on the right IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its left-hand side.
The presence checking operators ARE `ispresent`, `ischosen`, `isvalue` and `isbound`.
The result type of a presence checking operator IS `boolean`.
The operand of a presence checking operator MAY be of any type.

Special error-handling rules apply when the operand of a presence checking operator is a data object reference, function instance, template instance or the result of a `valueof` operation followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.

If resolving the dot notation, index notation or decoded field references of the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error (e.g. index out of range, sub-field of an omitted field), the normal error IS NOT raised and the following special handling applies instead.
If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error, no error IS produced.
If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error, evaluation of all remaining unresolved fields of the ExtendedFieldReference IS stopped.

If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error, all parts of the ExtendedFieldReference located to the right of the failing operation up to the end of the presence checking operator ARE NOT evaluated.
If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of its operand would produce an error, the presence checking operator IS evaluated to `false`.
The special error handling of dot notation, index notation and decoded field references in presence checking operators IS NOT applied recursively.

An error occurring while resolving the value of an index inside index notation or the value of an encoding format parameter of a decoded field reference IS NOT suppressed by the presence checking error-handling rule.
The `ispresent` operator checks whether a referenced field is present in a data object.
The `ispresent` operator has the syntax `ispresent "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
The `ispresent` operator returns `true` if its operand fulfils the `present` template restriction as described in clause 15.8.
The `ispresent` operator returns `false` if its operand does not fulfil the `present` template restriction.
When the operand of `ispresent` is a subfield of a template field to which AnyValue (`?`) is assigned, the template expansion mechanism of clause 15.6.2 IS applied before evaluating `ispresent`.
If `ispresent` applied to a template returns `true`, that template MAY be assigned to a non-optional field of the template's type in a template variable.
If `ispresent` applied to a template returns `true`, that template MAY be used as an actual parameter for a `template(present)` formal parameter or assigned to a `template(present)` variable.
The `ischosen` operator checks whether a referenced alternative is the one present in a data object.
The `ischosen` operator has the syntax `ischosen "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
The operand of the `ischosen` operator SHALL be a reference to an alternative of a union type or to a type alternative of an `anytype`.

The `ischosen` operator returns `true` if and only if the referenced alternative is the variant of the union type or the type alternative of the `anytype` that is actually selected in the given data object.
The `ischosen` operator returns `false` in all cases other than the referenced alternative being selected.
The `ischosen` operator IS applicable to data objects of union types or `anytype` that contain a specific value or a value list.
If the operand of `ischosen` is a value list, the operator returns `true` if all members of the value list have the referenced alternative selected.
The `ischosen` operator returns `false` if there is another alternative of the union type or `anytype` for which `ischosen` would return `true`.
When determining the selected alternative of an `anytype`, type compatibility IS NOT considered; only the exact type chosen for the value satisfies `ischosen`.
The `isvalue` operator checks whether a referenced data object is a specific value.
The `isvalue` operator has the syntax `isvalue "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
The `isvalue` operator returns `true` if its operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.
If the operand of `isvalue` is of a record or set type, an omitted optional field SHALL be considered as initialized.
If the operand of `isvalue` is of a record or set type, the operator SHALL also return `true` when optional fields of the operand are set to `omit` (all other fields being specific values).
The `isvalue` operator SHALL return `false` if its operand is not completely initialized or does not resolve to a specific value.
For the `isvalue` operator, the special value `null` IS considered a specific value.
`isvalue` applied to a union alternative IS different from `ischosen`: `isvalue` checks the content of the alternative, whereas `ischosen` checks whether the alternative has been selected.
The `isbound` operator checks whether a referenced data object is at least partially initialized.
The `isbound` operator has the syntax `isbound "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
The `isbound` operator returns `true` if its operand is at least partially initialized.
If the operand of `isbound` is of a record or set type, an omitted optional field SHALL be considered as initialized.
If the operand of `isbound` is of a record or set type, the operator SHALL return `true` if at least one optional field of the operand is set to `omit`.
The `isbound` operator SHALL return `false` if its operand is not at least partially initialized.
An inaccessible field (e.g. a non-selected alternative of a union, a subfield of an omitted record or set field, or a subfield of a non-selected union field) SHALL be considered as uninitialized.
The `isbound` operator SHALL return `false` for an inaccessible field.
For the `isbound` operator, the special value `null` IS considered a specific value.
If the operand of `isbound` is not a reference (e.g. `v_myRec.f1/0`), a runtime error raised while evaluating the operand IS NOT suppressed by the presence checking error-handling rule.
Within an expression, a field of a record or set type IS referenced with the dot notation `.field`.
An element of a `record of`, `set of`, array or string type IS referenced with the index notation `[index]`.
The dot `.` and the index brackets `[]` HAVE the same binding power.
Field references and list element references ARE evaluated from left to right.
A decoded field reference IS a specific notation called decoding notation.
The decoding notation SHALL only be applied to expressions of type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring` or `universal charstring`.
A decoded field reference IS used for accessing the content of implicitly decoded payload fields.
A decoded field reference has the syntax `ReferencedValue "=>" ( PredefinedType | TypeIdentifier | ( "(" Type [ "," Expression ] ")" ) )`.
The ReferencedValue preceding the `=>` symbol in a decoding notation SHALL be decoded into a value of the type following the `=>` symbol.
A failure of decoding in a decoding notation SHALL cause a test case error.
If the ReferencedValue is of `universal charstring` type and the extended syntax with parentheses is used, the Type MAY be followed by an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
The encoding format parameter of a decoding notation SHALL be of `charstring` type.
The encoding format parameter of a decoding notation SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function (clause C.5.4).
An encoding format parameter value other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
If the ReferencedValue is not of `universal charstring` type, the encoding format parameter SHALL NOT be present.
If the type following the `=>` symbol is not enclosed in parentheses, it SHALL be a built-in type or a type reference consisting of a single identifier.
An extended type reference following the `=>` symbol SHALL always use the extended syntax with parentheses.
A module IS the principal building block of TTCN-3.
A module MAY define a fully executable test suite or only a library of definitions.
A module MAY refer to the TTCN-3 language version and to the package versions it uses.
A module contains definitions.
A test suite IS a complete set of TTCN-3 modules containing test cases and a control part.
The transfer syntax of a TTCN-3 module SHALL be UTF-8, with each character of the module individually encoded and decoded according to UTF-8 as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646.
The encoded form of a TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT contain characters that do not correspond to any character of the module.
A module IS defined with the keyword `module`.
A module definition has the syntax `module` ModuleIdentifier [`language` FreeText {"," FreeText}] "{" [ModuleDefinitionsPart] "}".
A TTCN-3 module groups a set of (typically cohesive) TTCN-3 definitions.
A TTCN-3 module has an explicit import interface to use definitions from other TTCN-3 or non-TTCN-3 modules.
A definition in a TTCN-3 module CAN be hidden from other modules by means of visibility.
A TTCN-3 module CAN be compiled or interpreted separately.
A TTCN-3 module IS reusable.
A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable.
A module name SHALL be a TTCN-3 identifier.
The module identifier IS the informal text name of the module.
A module specification MAY carry an optional attribute, introduced by the `language` keyword, that identifies the edition of the TTCN-3 language in which the module is specified.
A language string identifying the core language edition SHALL be one of the listed strings "TTCN-3:2001" ... "TTCN-3:2023".
A module complying with the present document that carries a language string SHALL use the language string "TTCN-3:2023".
The optional `language` attribute of a module MAY identify the package versions used by the module.
The package tags ARE defined in ETSI ES 202 781, ES 202 782, ES 202 784, ES 202 785, ES 202 786, ES 203 022 and ES 203 790.
The language string and the package tags in the `language` attribute SHALL be written as a comma-separated list.
A module SHALL give at most one language string defining the core language version in which the module is defined.
For each extension package, a module SHALL use at most one extension package string of that extension package.
The module definitions part specifies the top-level definitions of the module.
The module definitions part MAY import visible identifiers from other modules.
Every module definition MAY be associated with attributes using the `with` statement.
A visible module definition MAY be imported by other modules.

The module definitions part IS a sequence of one or more module definitions, each consisting of an optional Visibility, one of TypeDef, ConstDef, TemplateDef, ModuleParDef, FunctionDef, SignatureDef, TestcaseDef, AltstepDef, ImportDef, GroupDef, ExtFunctionDef, FriendDef or ModuleControlDef, an optional WithStatement and an optional ";".
Definitions in the module definitions part MAY be made in any order.
A module definition CAN be evaluated at runtime.
Module definitions CAN be evaluated in any order.
A module definition SHALL be evaluated at the latest before the first reference to it.
A module definition that is not used NEED NOT be evaluated at all.
A top-level module definition outside of other scope units IS globally visible within the module.
A top-level module definition MAY be used elsewhere in the module.
An identifier imported from another module IS globally visible within the importing module and MAY be used elsewhere in it.
A declaration of a dynamic language element, such as a variable or a timer, SHALL only be made in a test case, function, altstep or component type.
A variable SHALL NOT be declared in the module definitions part (TTCN-3 has no global variables).
A component variable MAY be used by all test cases, functions and altsteps running on a component of that component type.
A module parameter IS a value or template that MAY be supplied by the test system at runtime.
The value of a module parameter IS NOT changed during test execution.
A module parameter MAY be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters and in template definitions.
A module parameter SHALL NOT be used within a type definition.
A module parameter declaration has the syntax [Visibility] `modulepar` [TemplateModifier] [TypeOrNestedTypeDef] Identifier [":=" TemplateBody] {"," Identifier [":=" TemplateBody]} ";".
A module parameter behaves at runtime as a global constant or as an unparameterized template.
Module parameterization IS restricted to value parameterization.
The actual values of module parameters SHALL be resolved statically at the start of runtime.
Module parameters allow a TTCN-3 test suite to be customized for a specific IUT, test setup or test campaign.
A module parameter declaration MAY specify a default value or template for the module parameter.
If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the default value or template given in the declaration SHALL be used during test execution.
If the test system provides an actual value or template for a module parameter, that actual value or template SHALL be used during test execution instead of the default.
The type of a module parameter IS either given explicitly or determined implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing.
When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the declaration IS omitted.
When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the type of the module parameter IS the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
If functions are used for the initialization of a module parameter, they SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
Initializing a module parameter with functions that do not follow the rules of clause 16.1.4 CAN cause non-deterministic test executions.
A visible module parameter MAY be imported.
An optional field of a record or set module parameter or module parameter field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or module parameter field, an `optional` attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with it, either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as the target of an assignment.
During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as an actual `out` or `inout` parameter.
A module parameter SHALL NOT be of port, default, timer or component type.
A module parameter SHALL NOT be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
A module parameter SHALL only be of the address type if the address type is explicitly defined within the module containing the module parameter declaration.
A module parameter SHALL be declared only within the module definitions part.
A module MAY contain more than one module parameter declaration.
A module parameter SHALL be declared only once, i.e. a module parameter SHALL NOT be redefined.
The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4.
The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration.
The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL conform to the TemplateModifier of the declaration.
If no TemplateModifier is present in a module parameter declaration, the TemplateBody SHALL resolve to a value.
A module parameter SHALL NOT be used in a type definition or array definition.
Every sub-element of component or default type of the default value of a module parameter SHALL be initialized with the special value `null`.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a module parameter declaration, the assignment part ":=" TemplateBody SHALL be present.
Definitions in the module definitions part MAY be collected in named groups.
Grouping of definitions IS done to aid readability and to add logical structure to the module.
If necessary to identify a sub-group uniquely within the group hierarchy (e.g. for the import of a specific sub-group), the dot notation SHALL be used.
A group definition has the syntax [`public`] `group` GroupIdentifier "{" {ModuleDefinition [";"]} "}".
A group of definitions MAY be specified wherever a single module definition is allowed.
A group MAY contain other groups (groups MAY be nested).
A group or nested group IS NOT a scope unit (groups have no scoping).
Attributes given to a group by an associated `with` statement apply to all elements of the group.
An import statement MAY import a group, so that all visible elements of the group are imported.
Group identifiers NEED NOT be unique across the whole module.
Top-level group identifiers of a module SHALL be unique.
The group identifiers of the direct sub-groups of a single group SHALL be unique.
Only public visibility SHALL be defined for a group (a group SHALL NOT be declared `private` or `friend`).
A group IS always public.
Visible definitions specified in a different module MAY be re-used by means of the import statement.
Every definition in a TTCN-3 module has an associated visibility.
The default visibility of a definition in a TTCN-3 module IS public.
A group IS public only.
Importing a group imports only the visible elements of the group.
An import statement MAY be used anywhere in the module definitions part.
An import statement has the syntax [Visibility] `import from` ModuleId [-> LocalModuleName] followed by either `all` [`except` "{" ExceptSpec "}"] or "{" ImportSpec "}", optionally terminated by ";".
An import statement MAY import module parameters, user-defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and testcases.
An importable definition IS composed of a name (its identifier), a specification and, for functions, altsteps and testcases, an associated behaviour description.
An import statement of a module MAY be explicitly imported by another module.
An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition or an import statement that is not visible from the importing module.
A module definition IS public by default.
An import statement IS private by default.
The behaviour description of an imported function, altstep or testcase IS NOT visible to the importer and has no effect on the import mechanism.

The specification part of an importable definition IS composed of local definitions (e.g. field names, enumerated values) and referenced definitions (e.g. references to types, templates, constants or module parameters).
A local definition IS an identifier that is newly defined in the importable definition.
A field name used in a template definition IS a referenced definition that is referenced via the type of the template.
A referenced definition IS itself an importable definition consisting of a name and a specification part with local and referenced definitions.
An importable definition CAN be built up recursively from other importable definitions.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported module parameter ARE the module parameter type.
The possible local definitions of an imported enumerated type ARE its enumerated values.
The possible local definitions of an imported structured type ARE its field names and nested type definitions.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported structured type ARE its field types.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported port type ARE its message types and signatures.
The possible local definitions of an imported component type ARE its constant names, variable names, timer names and port names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported component type ARE its constant types, variable types and port types.
The possible local definitions of an imported signature ARE its parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported signature ARE its parameter types, return type and exception types.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported constant ARE the constant type.
The possible local definitions of an imported data template ARE its formal parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported data template ARE its template type, formal parameter types, constants, module parameters and functions.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported signature template ARE its signature definition, constants, module parameters and functions.
The possible local definitions of an imported function ARE its formal parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported function ARE its formal parameter types, return type and the component type of its `runs on` clause.
The possible local definitions of an imported external function ARE its formal parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported external function ARE its formal parameter types and return type.
The possible local definitions of an imported altstep ARE its formal parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported altstep ARE its formal parameter types and the component type of its `runs on` clause.
The possible local definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter names.
The possible referenced definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter types and the component types of its `runs on` and `system` clauses.
The import mechanism distinguishes between the identifier of a referenced definition and the information necessary for the usage of the referenced definition within the imported definition.
The identifier of a referenced definition IS NOT imported automatically when the definition referencing it is imported.
If an imported definition has attributes defined by a `with` statement, the attributes SHALL also be imported.
A global attribute of a module IS associated with each definition of the module that does not have this attribute itself.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL resolve situations where the same definition is referred to more than once by import statements.
A definition referred to more than once by import statements (single definitions, groups, definitions of the same kind) SHALL be imported only once.
A TTCN-3 tool SHOULD provide mechanisms (e.g. overwriting, warnings to the user) to resolve multiple imports of the same definition.
Import statements and the definitions within import statements ARE treated independently one after the other in the order of their appearance.
A TTCN-3 module SHALL have its own name space.
Each definition in the name space of a module SHALL be uniquely identified.
A name clash CAN occur due to import, e.g. import from different modules.
A name clash caused by an imported definition SHALL be resolved by using the qualified name, i.e. prefixing the imported definition with the identifier of the module in which it is defined.
In a qualified name the module identifier prefix and the definition identifier SHALL be separated by a dot (".").

If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (component reference is a variable, a value returned from a function, or the type is given in the `runs on`, `mtc` or `system` clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in this component type.
In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value that clashes with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence over that definition.
In the context of an enumerated type, a definition of the importing module whose name clashes with an enumerated value SHALL be referenced by its qualified name.
If there is no ambiguity, an imported definition NEED NOT be prefixed with its module identifier when it is used.
If there is no ambiguity, an imported definition MAY be prefixed with its module identifier when it is used.
When a definition is referenced in the module where it is defined, the identifier of the current module MAY be used as prefix of the definition identifier.
Prefixing with the identifier of the current module SHALL only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.
An import statement MAY rename the imported module.
The new name given to a module renamed during import IS visible only in the importing module.
An import statement SHALL only be used in the module definitions part.
An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
An import statement SHALL import only top-level definitions of a module that are visible to the importing module.
An import statement SHALL NOT import a top-level definition that is invisible to the importing module.
An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition that occurs at a lower scope than the module (e.g. a local constant defined in a function).
An imported definition IS imported together with its name and all its local definitions.

A local definition (e.g. a field name of a record type or an enumerated value) has meaning only in the context of the definition in which it is defined; e.g. a field name of a record type IS usable only to access a field of that record type.
Importing an enumerated type IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

An imported definition IS imported together with all information of its referenced definitions that is necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions.
If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type defined in module A, the information necessary for the usage of that type IS automatically imported into module C.

If module C imports from module B global value or template definitions (constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (formal parameters, component constants and variables) of an enumerated type, the enumerated values of that type ARE implicitly imported into module C and are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C.
The implicit import of enumerated values IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

A referenced definition that is to be used in the importing module SHALL be explicitly imported, either directly from its source module or by importing the import statements of a module that imports it.
When a function, altstep or testcase is imported, its behaviour specification and all definitions used inside it ARE NOT visible to the importing module.
The language specification of an import statement SHALL NOT override the language specification of the importing module.
If the source module defines a language specification, the language specification of an import statement importing from it SHALL be identical to the language specification of the source module.
If the source module does not define a language specification, the language specification of the import statement IS taken as the language specification of the source module.
If the source module uses language concepts that are not part of the language specification taken from the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.
If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name IS NOT imported.
If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name SHALL NOT be used for referencing the imported module.
A module renamed in the import clause SHALL be referenced using its new local name only.
If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module SHALL be unique in the scope of the importing module.
Definitions with the same name defined in different modules ARE different definitions, even if their actual definitions are identical.
Importing a type that has the same name as a locally defined type results in two different types being available in the importing module.
A visible single definition MAY be imported by referring to its definition kind and its definition name(s).
An import of single definitions MAY be combined with imports of groups, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.

An import statement for single definitions has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( type {TypeDefIdentifier [","]} | template {TemplateIdentifier [","]} | const {ConstIdentifier [","]} | testcase {TestcaseIdentifier [","]} | altstep {AltstepIdentifier [","]} | function {FunctionIdentifier [","]} | signature {SignatureIdentifier [","]} | modulepar {ModuleParIdentifier [","]} ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
An import statement that imports a definition which is not visible to the importing module SHALL cause an error.
A single definition to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
A single definition to be imported SHALL be visible to the importing module.
A group of definitions MAY be imported.
An import of groups MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
A sub-group MAY be imported directly, without importing the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.
If the name of a sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module, the import statement SHALL use the dot notation to identify the sub-group uniquely.
If visible definitions of an imported group are not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of a group import.
The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of a group import excludes all definitions of that kind of the group from the import statement.
An import statement for groups has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [","] } ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
Importing a group IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of the group, including its sub-groups, except those listed in the except specification.
Import statements contained in an imported group or in its sub-groups ARE NOT part of the group import; only definitions are imported.
An except specification of an import statement IS NOT an exclusion of the listed definitions from being imported by other imports.
An import of all definitions of the same kind IS a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
An except specification excludes definitions only from the single list of definitions of the import to which it belongs.
A group to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
The `all` keyword MAY be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.
The `all` keyword used with the `const` keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the module definitions part of the module referenced by the import statement.

The `all` keyword used with the `function` keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions and the visible module control part of the module referenced by the import statement.
If visible definitions of a kind are to be excluded from an import of all definitions of that kind, their identifiers SHALL be listed following the `except` keyword.
An import of definitions of the same kind MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of groups and imports of import statements.

An import statement for definitions of the same kind has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( Kind all [ except { Identifier [","] } ] ) [";"] } "}" [";"], where Kind is one of type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
Importing definitions of the same kind IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except those listed in the except specification.
An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
An import statement MAY import all visible definitions of the module definitions part of a module by using the `all` keyword next to the module name.

If visible definitions are not to be imported by an import of all definitions of a module, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of an import of all definitions of a module.
The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of an import of all definitions excludes all visible declarations of that kind from the import statement.
An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
An import of all definitions of a module imports only the definitions declared directly in that module, including the address type and the module control part if they are specified.
An import of all definitions of a module DOES NOT import the import statements of that module.

An import statement for all definitions of a module has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId all [ { except "{" ( Kind { Identifier [","] } | all ) ... "}" [";"] } ] [";"], where Kind is one of group, type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
Importing all visible definitions of a module IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except those listed in the except specification.

An import statement that imports all visible definitions of a module with the `all` keyword SHALL NOT contain any other form of import (import of single definitions, import of definitions of the same kind, etc.).
The except specification of an import of all definitions SHALL contain at most one except entry per kind of definition (group, type, etc.).

An import statement that imports visible definitions from a module of another TTCN-3 edition or from a non-TTCN-3 source SHALL use the language specification to denote the language, optionally with a version number, of the source.
A language specification consists of the `language` keyword followed by a textual declaration of the denoted language.
The language specification of an import statement MAY be omitted when importing from a TTCN-3 module of the same edition as the importing module.
A language specification denoting a TTCN-3 edition SHALL use the TTCN-3 language identifiers defined in clause 8.1.
A language specification MAY additionally use the package identifiers defined in ETSI ES 202 781, ETSI ES 202 782, ETSI ES 202 784 and ETSI ES 202 785.

When an incompatibility is discovered between the language or package identification (including implicit identification by omitting the language specification) and the syntax of the module from which definitions are imported, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL make a reasonable effort to resolve the conflict.
An import statement has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleIdentifier [LanguageSpec] ... [";"], where the optional language specification follows the module identifier.
A versioned element IS an element defined in another TTCN-3 edition that is referenced from within a TTCN-3 module.
A foreign element IS an element defined in a language other than TTCN-3 that is referenced from within a TTCN-3 module.
A versioned or foreign element SHALL NOT be used in a TTCN-3 module of a given edition unless it has a TTCN-3 view in that edition.
When the definition of a TTCN-3 element is based on another TTCN-3 element, the information content of the referenced element SHALL be available and IS used for the new definition.
When a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of the fields of that type SHALL be accessible and are used for the template definition.
A versioned or foreign element used as the type of a TTCN-3 definition SHALL provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.
A versioned or foreign element CAN contain more information than required by TTCN-3.
The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element IS that part of the information carried by the element which is necessary to use it in TTCN-3.
The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element IS the full set or a subset of the information content of that element and IS NOT a superset of it.
A versioned or foreign element CAN have no TTCN-3 view, so that no TTCN-3 definition in the given edition can be based on it.
A zero TTCN-3 view IS the absence of a TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element in a given edition.
The names of versioned or foreign element declarations SHALL be imported, like definitions of other TTCN-3 modules of the given edition, to make them visible in a TTCN-3 module.
When a versioned or foreign element is imported, only its TTCN-3 view IS seen from the importing TTCN-3 module.
An import statement that imports from a TTCN-3 module of another edition or from a non-TTCN-3 module SHALL contain an appropriate language identifier string.
A versioned or foreign element without a TTCN-3 view of a given edition SHALL NOT be imported into a TTCN-3 module of that edition.
When importing is done with the `all` directive, the TTCN-3 tool SHALL automatically select all importable objects.
An import statement MAY import elements by listing the names of the elements to be imported.
An import statement that lists the names of elements to be imported SHALL list only importable elements.

With an implicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions ARE mapped internally in the TTCN-3 tool to TTCN-3 definitions as defined by the language mapping, and the importing module works with the internal representations of the imported definitions.

With an explicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions ARE mapped directly to separate TTCN-3 definitions, and the importing module imports the generated TTCN-3 and works with the mapped TTCN-3 definitions.

In the first option, the import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool uses the internal representation of the implicit mapping of the module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

In the second option, the import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool imports from a TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

In the third option, the import statement imports the explicit TTCN-3 representation of the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool imports the TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module according to the language mapping specification of that language.
The language specification of an import statement SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and its TTCN-3 version is known.
A definition imported from a non-TTCN-3 language source has public visibility by default, unless the respective language mapping defines other rules.
The import mechanism IS designed to allow the re-use of definitions from other TTCN-3 editions or from non-TTCN-3 language sources.
The rules for importing definitions from specifications written in other languages, e.g. SDL packages, MAY follow the TTCN-3 rules or MAY be defined separately.
A visible import statement of a TTCN-3 module MAY be imported by other TTCN-3 modules.
An import of import statements has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleIdentifier [LanguageSpec] "{" import all [";"] "}" [";"].
Importing the import statements of a module re-imports the import statements of that module into the importing module.
If module B imports the import statements of module A, everything that A imports using import statements visible to B IS also imported by B.

Import of import statements IS transitive: if module C imports all import statements of module B, which imports the import statements of module A, then C imports everything A imports, provided the import statements are visible to B and C.
An individual import statement of another module SHALL NOT be imported; only all visible import statements can be imported.
An import of import statements MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of groups and imports of definitions of the same kind.
Import statements SHALL NOT be imported from a non-TTCN-3 module.
The language specification of an import of import statements SHALL denote a TTCN-3 edition only and not a non-TTCN-3 language.

When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module SHALL be compatible according to the rules of clause 8.2.3.8.
A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition MAY import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists.
A definition or import statement IS imported according to the language specification of the module in which the definition or import statement is defined.
If the module in which the definitions or import statements are defined has no language specification, the language specification of the import statement that imports them IS used instead.

If both the module in which the imported definitions or import statements are defined and the import statement importing them have a language specification, these language specifications SHALL be identical.
If neither the defining module nor the import statement has a language specification, the language specification IS determined from other sources in a tool-specific way.
A TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT import from a later TTCN-3 edition than its own; it SHALL import only from earlier or the same editions.
The TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement SHALL be lower than or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
A module MAY define other modules to be its friend modules.
A friend module declaration has the syntax [private] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";".
Friendship to modules IS defined by the exporting module, which declares the definitions, and IS NOT defined by the importing module.
Friendship between modules MAY be cyclic.
If a module is a friend of a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with `public` and `friend` visibility ARE visible to the friend module.
For a non-friend importing module, only `public` top-level definitions ARE visible.
A friend module declaration that references a missing module SHALL NOT cause an error.
A TTCN-3 tool MAY check friend modules.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL NOT issue more than a warning if a friend module is missing.
A friend module declaration SHALL have only `private` visibility, if any visibility is specified.
A friend module declaration IS always private.
A top-level module definition HAS a visibility.
An import statement HAS a visibility.
The visibility of a top-level module definition or an import statement MAY be set explicitly by a visibility modifier.
A top-level module definition without an explicit visibility modifier IS public by default, except for imported definitions and friend definitions.
An import statement without an explicit visibility modifier IS private by default.
A friend definition IS private only.
A group definition IS public only.
A group definition SHALL NOT be declared with `friend` or `private` visibility.
A visibility modifier HAS the syntax [ `public` | `friend` | `private` ], i.e. it is optional and is one of the keywords `public`, `friend` or `private`.
The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement CONTROLS whether it is importable by another module.
The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement IS one of three visibilities: public, friend or private.
A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility IS importable by any other module.
A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility IS importable by friend modules only.
A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility SHALL NOT be imported by any other module.

When an importable definition is imported, all information of referenced definitions necessary for the usage of the importable definition IS imported together with it, even if a referenced definition is private.
The identifier of a private referenced definition IS NOT visible in the importing module.
The visibility of a group IS always public.
The visibility of an imported definition IS private by default.
A module definition other than a group or an imported definition IS public by default.
The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement DEFINES its importability by another module.
Membership of a top-level definition or an import statement in a group IS NOT affecting the importability of that definition.
The module control part IS a shorthand notation to define a module control function.
The module control part HAS the syntax `control` StatementBlock.
The module control part IS equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no `runs on` clause and no `return` clause.
A module definition with public visibility IS importable directly by a non-friend module.
A module definition with public visibility IS importable directly by a friend module.
A module definition with public visibility IS importable via group import by a non-friend module.
A module definition with public visibility IS importable via group import by a friend module.
A module definition with friend visibility IS NOT importable directly by a non-friend module.
A module definition with friend visibility IS importable directly by a friend module.
A module definition with friend visibility IS NOT importable via group import by a non-friend module.
A module definition with friend visibility IS importable via group import by a friend module.
A module definition with private visibility IS NOT importable directly by a non-friend module.
A module definition with private visibility IS NOT importable directly by a friend module.
A module definition with private visibility IS NOT importable via group import by a non-friend module.
A module definition with private visibility IS NOT importable via group import by a friend module.
An import statement with public visibility IS imported by a non-friend module.
An import statement with public visibility IS imported by a friend module.
An import statement with friend visibility IS NOT imported by a non-friend module.
An import statement with friend visibility IS imported by a friend module.
An import statement with private visibility IS NOT imported by a non-friend module.
An import statement with private visibility IS NOT imported by a friend module.
A TTCN-3 module CAN contain at most one module control part.
When not used as an entry point for test suite execution, a module control function CAN be invoked explicitly like a function, using the `control` keyword instead of an identifier.
In an explicit invocation of a module control function, the `control` keyword MAY be prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.
If the referenced module control function has no parameters, the parameter list MAY be omitted at the place of invocation.
A test configuration IS a concurrent test configuration whose specification in TTCN-3 MAY be dynamic.
A test configuration IS a set of inter-connected test components with well-defined communication ports and an explicit test system interface.
The test system interface IS the entity that defines the borders of the test system.
A test configuration SHALL contain exactly one Main Test Component (MTC).
A test component that is not the MTC IS a parallel test component (PTC).
The MTC SHALL be created automatically by the test system at the start of each test case execution.
The behaviour defined in the body of a test case SHALL execute on the MTC.
During test case execution, test components other than the MTC CAN be created dynamically by explicit use of the `create` operation.
Test case execution SHALL end when the MTC terminates.
A PTC IS NOT in an explicit hierarchical relationship with any other PTC.
The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating any other test component.
The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating the MTC.
When the MTC terminates, the test system SHALL stop all PTCs that are not yet terminated when the test case execution ends.
Communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface IS performed via communication ports.
A component type (keyword `component`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
A port type (keyword `port`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
The actual test configuration of test components and the connections between them IS established by performing `create` and `connect` operations within the test case behaviour.
A port of a test component IS connected to a port of the test system interface by means of the `map` operation.
A connection among test components and between a test component and the test system interface IS port-oriented, i.e. established between ports.
A port IS modelled as an infinite FIFO queue.
A port queue IS storing the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the test component owning that port.
A port of a real test system CAN overflow although TTCN-3 ports are infinite in principle.
An overflow of a port in a real test system SHALL be treated as a test case error.
A TTCN-3 connection IS either a port-to-port connection or a port-to-test system interface connection.
A test component MAY maintain any number of connections.
A one-to-many connection MAY be established.
A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with more than one port owned by the same test component.
A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by another test component B.
A port owned by a test component SHALL have at most a one-to-one connection with the test system interface, i.e. it SHALL NOT be connected to more than one port of the test system interface.
A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with another port of the test system interface.
A port that is connected SHALL NOT be mapped.
A port that is mapped SHALL NOT be connected.
The restrictions on connections CANNOT always be checked at compile-time, because TTCN-3 allows dynamic configurations and addresses.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check the restrictions on connections at runtime.
A failing runtime check of a connection restriction SHALL lead to a test case error.
The object being tested IS the Implementation Under Test (IUT).
An IUT CAN offer direct interfaces for testing.
When the IUT is part of a system, the tested object IS the System Under Test (SUT).
In the minimal case the IUT and the SUT ARE equivalent.
The term SUT IS used in the standard to mean either SUT or IUT.
The specification of the real physical connection to the SUT IS NOT within the scope of TTCN-3.
A well-defined abstract test system interface SHALL be associated with each test case.
A test system interface definition IS identical to a component type definition.
A test system interface IS a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.
The test system interface IS statically defining the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.
A connection between the test system interface and a test component IS dynamic.
A connection between the test system interface and a test component MAY be modified during a test run by using `map` and `unmap` operations.
A component type definition IS used to define the test system interface.
A component type definition and a test system interface definition ARE conceptually of the same form, both being collections of ports defining possible connection points.
When a component type is used as a test system interface, the test system interface CANNOT make use of the constants, variables and timers declared in that component type.
A test system interface definition HAS the same syntax as a component type definition.
A test case using more than one test component SHALL be associated with a component type reference defining the test system interface.
The ports of the test system interface SHALL be instantiated automatically by the test system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.
The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
The `system` operation SHALL be used to address the ports of the test system interface.
When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, a test system interface NEED NOT be associated to the test case.
When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, the component type associated with the MTC IS implicitly defining the test system interface.
A variable, timer or constant declared in a component type that is used as test system interface IS without effect.
A test system interface definition SHALL satisfy the same restrictions as a component type definition.
A TTCN-3 constant IS a runtime constant.
After value assignment, a constant SHALL NOT change its value during test execution.
A constant MAY be used on the right hand side of an assignment, in an expression, in an actual parameter and in a template definition.
A constant used within a type definition SHALL have a value known at compile-time.

A constant declaration has the syntax `const` [TypeOrNestedTypeDef] followed by one or more ConstIdentifier [ArrayDef] ":=" ConstantExpression items optionally separated by ",", optionally terminated by ";".
A constant IS a name assigned to a fixed value.
A value SHALL be assigned to a constant only once, at the place of the constant declaration.
A constant SHALL NOT change its value during test execution.
A constant SHALL be defined only once in a TTCN-3 module.
A constant MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
The type of a constant IS either provided explicitly or determined implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing.
When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the constant declaration IS missing.
When automatic typing is used, the type of a constant IS equal to the type of the expression on the right hand side of the assignment.
A function used for the initialization of a constant SHOULD adhere to the rules for deterministic functions defined in clause 16.1.4.
Using a function for the initialization of a constant that does not adhere to the rules of clause 16.1.4 CAN cause non-deterministic test execution.
An optional field of a record or set constant or of a constant field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a constant or a constant field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with the constant or constant field either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.

A constant expression initializing a constant that is used in a type or array definition SHALL only contain literals, predefined functions except `rnd`, operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of clause 10.
A constant expression initializing a constant that is used in a type or array definition SHALL NOT contain a call of the predefined function `rnd`.
The only value that can be assigned to a global constant of default, component, port or timer type, or to a component constant of default or component type, IS the special value `null`.
Referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` using dot notation or index notation SHALL cause an error.
The right hand side of the assignment that initializes a constant SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
The ConstantExpression of a constant declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is type compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a constant declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a constant declaration, the assignment part (":=" ConstantExpression) SHALL be present.
A TTCN-3 variable IS a statically typed variable.
A variable IS either a value variable, which stores values, or a template variable, which stores templates.

A variable MAY be of a simple basic type, a basic string type, a structured type, a special data type (including subtypes derived from these types), an address type, a component type, a default type, a port type or a timer type.
The type of a variable IS provided either explicitly in the declaration or implicitly according to the automatic typing rules of clause 6.5.
When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of a variable declaration IS absent.
When automatic typing is used, the type of a variable IS equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment in its declaration.
A variable MAY be declared and used in testcases, functions and altsteps.
A variable MAY be declared in a component type definition.
A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions running on that component type.
A variable MAY be declared lazy using the `@lazy` modifier.
A variable MAY be declared fuzzy using the `@fuzzy` modifier as an alternative to the `@lazy` modifier.
A variable declaration SHALL NOT contain both the `@lazy` and the `@fuzzy` modifier.
A variable declared `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` MAY additionally be declared with the `@deterministic` modifier.
The `@deterministic` modifier on a lazy or fuzzy variable IS an indication that, in a deterministic evaluation context, any evaluation of the variable has no side effect and yields the same result.
The lazy or fuzzy property of a variable IS valid only in the scope where the variable name is visible.
A fuzzy variable passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier IS not fuzzy inside the called function.
A fuzzy variable passed to a lazy formal parameter IS lazy within the called function.

Whenever a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the test execution SHALL save the lexical environment (the set of directly or indirectly referenced values and templates) valid at the time of the assignment, so that the expression can be resolved when the lazy or fuzzy value or template is evaluated.

If a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned in a lower scope than the scope of its evaluation, saving the lexical environment IS extending the lifetime of the referenced variables defined in that lower scope.
A TTCN-3 value variable IS a variable that stores values.
A value variable declaration IS the `var` keyword followed by a type identifier or a nested type definition and a variable identifier.
A value variable declaration MAY assign an initial value to the value variable.
A value variable MAY be used on the right hand side and on the left hand side of assignments.
A value variable MAY be used in expressions.
A value variable MAY be used following the `return` keyword in the body of a function with a return clause in its header.
A value variable MAY be passed as actual parameter to both value formal parameters and template-type formal parameters.

A value variable declaration has the syntax `var` [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] followed by one or more comma-separated VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" Expression ] and an optional ";".
A value variable IS an association of a name with the location of a value.
A value variable MAY change its value several times during test execution.
A value MAY be assigned several times to a value variable.
A value variable MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
The Expression in a value variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef.
A value variable SHALL store values only.
A value variable SHALL NOT be declared or used in a module definitions part.
A global variable IS NOT supported in TTCN-3.
Use of an uninitialized value variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy value variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy value variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.

If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.

If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in a deterministic context, the expression assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable MAY contain a direct or indirect reference to that variable.
Evaluation of an expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable that directly or indirectly references that variable SHALL cause a dynamic error.
Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
The Expression in a value variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is at least partially initialized.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a value variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a value variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" Expression) SHALL be present.
A value variable of timer type IS assignable from a timer.
A TTCN-3 template variable IS a variable that stores templates.
A template variable declaration IS the `var template` keywords followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable.
A template variable MAY store matching mechanisms in addition to values.
A template variable MAY be used on the right hand side and on the left hand side of assignments.
A template variable MAY be used following the `return` keyword in the body of a function that defines a template-type return value in its header.
A template variable MAY be passed as actual parameter to a template-type formal parameter.
A template instance MAY be assigned to a template variable or to a field of a template variable.

A template variable declaration has the syntax `var` TemplateModifier [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] followed by one or more comma-separated VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody and an optional ";".
A template variable IS an association of a name with the location of a template or a value.
Every value IS also a template.
A template variable MAY change its template several times during test execution.
A template or value MAY be assigned several times to a template variable.
A template variable MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
The content of a template variable MAY be restricted by a template restriction to the matching mechanisms specific value and `omit`, in the same way as formal template parameters.
The template restriction `template (omit)` MAY be replaced by the shorthand notation `omit`.
A string type template or a list type template CAN be concatenated.
A template variable SHALL NOT be declared or used in a module definitions part.
A template variable used on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL NOT be an operand of a TTCN-3 operator.
If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.
When an element of a template variable is accessed on the left hand side or the right hand side of an assignment, the rules of clause 15.6 SHALL apply.
The dot notation and the index notation MAY be used to inspect and modify fields of a template variable, although TTCN-3 operations SHALL NOT be applied directly to template variables.
Use of an uninitialized template variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
If a template variable is restricted, the template used to initialize it SHALL contain only the matching mechanisms permitted by the restriction as described in clause 15.8.
A template variable SHALL be completely initialized in order to be used in a sending or receiving operation, as global and local templates.
The restrictions on templates given in clause 15.0 SHALL apply to template variables.
The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.

If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.

If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context, the template body assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the declared template variable.
The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" TemplateBody) SHALL be present.
A fuzzy template variable IS evaluated on every usage.
The TTCN-3 language IS a language that provides a timer mechanism.
A timer MAY be declared and used in a test case, a function or an altstep.
A timer MAY be declared in a component type definition.
A timer declared in a component type definition MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep that runs on that component type.
A timer declaration MAY assign a default duration value to the timer.
When a timer is started without a specified timer value, the timer SHALL be started with its default duration value.
A timer value SHALL be a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
The base unit of a timer value IS seconds.
A timer array MAY be declared.
The default durations of the elements of a timer array SHALL be assigned using a value array.
A default duration assignment of a timer array SHALL use the array value notation.
If the default duration of an element of a timer array is to be skipped, the element SHALL be explicitly marked with the not used symbol ("-") in the default duration value array.
A timer declaration has the syntax `timer` followed by one or more TimerIdentifier [ArrayDef] ":=" TimerValue items separated by optional commas, optionally terminated by ";".
A timer IS local to a component.
A component CAN start a timer, stop a timer, check whether a timer is running, read the elapsed time of a running timer and process timeout events after timer expiration.
A timer value IS interpreted with a base unit of seconds.

A timer declared and started in a scope unit (e.g. a function) ceases to exist when the scope unit is left, unless a constant, variable or parameter of the current or a higher scope unit or of an activated altstep contains a reference to the timer.

A timer declared in a left scope unit IS kept in existence as long as at least one constant, variable or parameter of the current or a higher scope unit or an activated altstep contains a reference to the timer.
A timer that ceased to exist stops running.
A timer that ceased to exist IS NOT able to time out.
A timer that ceased to exist CANNOT be referenced via the `any timer` or `all timer` constructs.
Unless stated otherwise, a timer IS semantically equivalent to a constant of a timer type.
A timer that ceased to exist IS NOT a contributor to the test behaviour.
The default duration value of a single timer SHALL resolve to a non-negative numerical `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
The default duration value of a single timer SHALL NOT be `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
The default duration value of a timer array SHALL resolve to an array of non-negative numerical `float` values (not `infinity` or `not_a_number`).
The default duration array of a timer array SHALL have the same size as the timer array.
The TTCN-3 language IS able to send and receive simple or complex messages over message-based ports defined by the test configuration.
A message CAN be a message explicitly concerned with testing the SUT or an internal co-ordination and control message specific to the test configuration.
A message IS an instance of a type declared in the `in`, `out` or `inout` clause of a message port type definition.
Any type MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.
A value of any basic type or structured type MAY be sent or received as a message.
A template used to receive a message MAY be declared as a combination of values and matching mechanisms.
A message MAY be declared by a global, local or in-line template.
A message MAY be constructed and passed via a variable or a template variable.
A message MAY be passed via a value formal parameter or a template formal parameter.
A signature IS the short name of a procedure signature.
Procedure-based communication SHALL be based on procedure signatures.
Procedure-based communication MAY be used for the communication among test components within the test system.
Procedure-based communication MAY be used for the communication between the test system and the SUT.

If procedure-based communication is used between the test system and the SUT, a remote procedure MAY be invoked either in the SUT (the test system performs the call) or in the test system (the SUT performs the call).

A signature definition has the syntax `signature` SignatureIdentifier "(" { [ `in` | `inout` | `out` ] Type ValueParIdentifier [","] } ")" [ ( `return` TypeOrNestedTypeDef ) | `noblock` ] [ `exception` "(" ExceptionTypeList ")" ].
A procedure signature SHALL be defined in the TTCN-3 module for every procedure used for procedure-based communication among test components, called from the SUT or called from the test system.
The TTCN-3 language supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.
A signature definition without the `noblock` keyword IS used for blocking procedure-based communication.
A signature definition MAY have signature parameters.
A signature parameter SHALL be of a data type only, i.e. of a basic type, a structured type thereof or a subtype thereof.
The parameter list of a signature definition MAY include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction (`in`, `out` or `inout`).
A signature parameter with direction `inout` or `out` IS used to retrieve information from the remote procedure.
The direction of a signature parameter IS as seen by the called party rather than by the calling party.
A remote procedure MAY return a value after its termination.
The return type of a signature SHALL be a data type only.
If a remote procedure returns a value, the type of the return value SHALL be specified by a `return` clause in the corresponding signature definition.
An exception that may be raised by a remote procedure IS represented as a value of a specific type.
A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check an exception raised by a remote procedure.
The conversion of exceptions generated by or sent to the SUT into the corresponding TTCN-3 type or SUT representation IS tool and system specific and outside the scope of the TTCN-3 core language.
The exceptions of a signature ARE defined in the form of an exception list included in the signature definition.
The exception list of a signature definition IS the set of all possible types of the exceptions that the remote procedure may raise.
The meaning of an exception IS usually distinguished only by specific values of the exception type.
A signature definition for non-blocking communication SHALL use the `noblock` keyword.
A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword SHALL only have `in` parameters.
A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword SHALL NOT have a return value.
A signature definition with the `noblock` keyword MAY have an exception list.
A signature parameter SHALL be of a data type.
The return type of a signature SHALL be a data type.
A template IS used either to transmit a set of distinct values or to test whether a set of received values matches the template specification.
A template MAY be defined globally or locally.
A template IS a way to organize and re-use test data, including a simple form of inheritance.
A template MAY be parameterized.
A template MAY contain matching mechanisms.
A template MAY be used with message-based communication or with procedure-based communication.
A template MAY specify values, ranges and matching attributes, which MAY then be used in both message-based and procedure-based communication.
A template MAY be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.
A type-based (message) template IS used for message-based communication.
A signature template IS used for procedure-based communication.
A template declaration MAY contain the `@fuzzy` modifier to declare the template as fuzzy.
When a fuzzy template is used from a non-fuzzy template, the fuzzy template IS evaluated.
For an unparameterized non-fuzzy template, the result of a fuzzy template used in it IS the same for every usage of the non-fuzzy template.
