A fuzzy template declaration MAY contain the `@deterministic` modifier to declare the template as deterministic.
A deterministic template SHALL evaluate to the same result whenever it is evaluated in the same deterministic evaluation context.
A modified template declaration IS a partial specification that specifies only the fields to be changed from the base template.
A template SHALL be specified only for a component data type or a procedure signature.
The expression or template body initializing a template SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the template being declared.
The expression or template body initializing a template SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized, or to a matching mechanism.
The body of a fuzzy template SHALL NOT contain calls of functions that have `inout` or `out` parameters.
A function called from the body of a fuzzy template MAY internally call other functions that have `inout` or `out` parameters.
The fuzzy feature of a fuzzy template IS valid only in the scope where the name of the template is visible.
When a fuzzy template is passed to a formal template parameter declared without a modifier, the fuzzy template IS treated as non-fuzzy inside the called function.
The template body of a fuzzy template that is declared `@deterministic` SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
Every usage of a fuzzy template whose body is a function call IS a re-evaluation of the function call.
An instance of a message with actual values MAY be specified using a template.
A template IS a set of instructions to build a message for sending or to match a received message.
A template used in a `send` operation IS the complete set of field values comprising the message to be transmitted over a port.
In a template used for sending, an omitted optional field IS a value notation and not a matching mechanism.
A template used in a `receive`, `trigger` or `check` operation IS the data template against which an incoming message is matched.
A template used for receiving MAY contain the matching mechanisms defined in clauses 15.6.6, 15.8 and annex B.
A template used in a receiving operation SHALL NOT have incoming values bound to it.
At the time of a `send` operation, the used template SHALL be completely initialized.
At the time of a `send` operation, every field of the used template SHALL resolve to an actual value or to `omit`.
At the time of a `send` operation, a field of the used template SHALL NOT contain, directly or indirectly, any matching mechanism other than `omit`.
At the time of a receiving operation, the matching template SHALL be completely initialized.
An optional field of a record or set template or template field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a template or template field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with the template or template field, either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
A template of type integer with the value list (1, 2, 3) used in a receiving operation matches only the integer values 1, 2 and 3.
An instance of a procedure parameter list with actual values MAY be specified using a template.
A template MAY be defined for any procedure by referencing the associated signature definition.
A signature template IS a definition of the values and matching mechanisms of the procedure parameters only, and IS NOT a definition of the return value.
The value or matching mechanism for the return value of a procedure SHALL be defined within the `reply` or `getreply` operation.

A signature template used in a `call` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `in` and `inout` parameters, and a signature template used in a `reply` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `out` and `inout` parameters.
At the time of a `call` operation, every `in` and `inout` parameter in the signature template SHALL resolve to an actual value.
At the time of a `call` operation, the `in` and `inout` parameter fields of the signature template SHALL NOT contain matching mechanisms, either directly or indirectly.
In a signature template used in a `call` operation, the template specification for an `out` parameter IS ignored.
In a signature template used in a `call` operation, an `out` parameter field MAY contain a matching mechanism or MAY be omitted.
A signature template used in a `getcall` operation IS the data template against which the incoming parameter fields are matched.
A signature template used in a `getcall` operation MAY contain the matching mechanisms defined in annex B.
A signature template used in a `getcall` operation SHALL NOT have incoming values bound to it.
In the matching process of a `getcall` operation, every `out` parameter SHALL be ignored.
At the time of a `call`, `reply` or `raise` operation, the used signature template SHALL be completely initialized.
At the time of a `call` operation, every `in` and `inout` parameter of the used signature template SHALL resolve to a specific value or to `omit`.
At the time of a `reply` or `raise` operation, every `out` and `inout` parameter of the used signature template SHALL resolve to a specific value or to `omit`.

At the time of a `call`, `reply` or `raise` operation, the parameters that have to resolve to specific values (`in`/`inout` in a call, `out`/`inout` in a reply or raise) SHALL NOT contain, directly or indirectly, any matching mechanism other than `omit`.

The NotUsedSymbol SHALL be used only in signature templates for parameters that are not relevant, and in modified template declarations and modified in-line templates to indicate no change for the specified field or element.
At the time of a `getcall`, `getreply` or `catch` operation, the matching template SHALL be completely initialized.
An optional field of a record or set parameter or parameter field of a signature template MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

For implicit initialization of a parameter or parameter field of a signature template, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
The values of `out` and `inout` parameters returned by a `call` operation IS NOT returned by the template and are retrieved using an assignment clause at the end of the call statement.
In a `getreply` operation, the `in` parameters of the signature template IS ignored in matching.
A TTCN-3 module MAY define global templates and local templates.

A global or local template declaration has the syntax `template` [TemplateRestriction] [`@fuzzy`] [`@deterministic`] [`@abstract`] Type TemplateIdentifier ["(" TemplateFormalParList ")"] [`modifies` TemplateRef] ":=" BaseTemplateBody.
A global template SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
A local template SHALL be defined in a testcase, function, altstep or statement block.
A global or local template SHALL adhere to the scoping rules specified in clause 5.
A global or local template MAY be parameterized.
An actual parameter of a template MAY be a value or a template.
The formal and actual parameter lists of a template SHALL follow the rules defined in clause 5.2.
A global or local template IS initialized at the place of its declaration.
At the place of declaration of a template, every template field that is not affected by parameterization SHALL receive a value or matching mechanism.
A template field affected by parameterization IS initialized at the time of template use.
A function used for the initialization of a template SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
A function used for template initialization that does not follow the rules of clause 16.1.4 CAN cause non-deterministic test execution.

At the time of use of a template (e.g. in `send`, `receive`, `call`, `getcall`), the template fields MAY be changed by in-line modified templates, values MAY be passed in via value parameters, and templates MAY be passed in via template parameters.
A change of template fields made at the time of use (by in-line modification or parameter passing) IS NOT persistent in the template after the corresponding communication event.
The dot notation (e.g. myTemplateId.fieldId) SHALL NOT be used to set or retrieve values in templates in communication events.
The "->" symbol SHALL be used to retrieve values from templates in communication events.
Referencing elements of templates or template fields IS subject to the restrictions described in clause 15.6.
A function used in expressions specifying templates or template fields IS subject to the restrictions specified in clause 16.1.4.
After completing initialization, a global or local message template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL be completely initialized.

After completing initialization, a global or local signature template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL fulfil at least one of the following: all procedure parameters are completely initialized; or all `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol; or all `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol.
A signature template whose procedure parameters are all completely initialized IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
A signature template in which all `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
A signature template whose `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol MAY be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.
A signature template whose `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol SHALL NOT be used in `reply` and `getreply` operations.
A signature template in which all `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
A signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol MAY be used in `reply` and `getreply` operations.
A signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.
The initialization of a template without parameters IS completed at the place of its declaration.
The initialization of a parameterized template IS completed at the time of its use.
A template MAY be specified directly at the place where it is used.
A template specified directly at the place where it is used IS called an in-line template.
An in-line template IS written as an optional type followed by a colon, followed by a TemplateBody ([ Type ":" ] TemplateBody).

An in-line template IS an argument of a communication operation or an actual parameter of a testcase, function or altstep call, and is therefore always placed within parentheses and potentially separated by a comma.
An in-line template MAY be defined directly at the place of its use.
An in-line template IS NOT named.
An in-line template CANNOT be referenced or reused.
The lifetime of an in-line template IS the TTCN-3 statement (assignment, testcase/function/altstep invocation, return from a function, or communication operation) in which it is defined.
The type of an in-line template SHOULD only be omitted when the type is implicitly unambiguous.
For a literal in-line template, the type MAY be omitted if it is integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring or octetstring.
The type of a constant, parameter or variable of the actual scope IS always unambiguous and therefore MAY always be omitted in an in-line template.

An in-line template containing matching mechanisms instead of or inside values SHALL only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (`receive`, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`), in arguments of the `match` operation and `select case` statement, in actual template parameters, on the right hand side of assignments to template variables, and in return statements of template returning functions.
An in-line template not containing matching mechanisms MAY be defined wherever values are allowed.
When an in-line template is used in a communication operation, the type of the in-line template SHALL be in the list of types of the port over which the template is sent or received.

If there is an ambiguity between a type listed in the port type and the type of the value provided (e.g. through subtyping), the type name of the in-line template SHALL be included in the communication operation.
A function used in an expression when specifying an in-line template or template field SHALL obey the restrictions specified in clause 16.1.4.
A new template MAY be specified as a modified template of an existing template.
A modified template IS a template that specifies modifications to particular fields of the original template, either directly or indirectly.
An in-line modified template MAY be defined in addition to explicitly named modified templates.

A global or local modified template IS declared as `template` [TemplateRestriction] [`@fuzzy`] [`@deterministic`] [`@abstract`] Type TemplateIdentifier ["(" TemplateFormalParList ")"] `modifies` (TemplateRef | BaseTemplateBody) ":=" BaseTemplateBody.
An in-line modified template IS written as `modifies` BaseTemplateBody ":=" BaseTemplateBody.
The `modifies` keyword denotes the parent template from which the modified template is derived.
The parent template of a modified template MAY be an original (unmodified) template, a modified template or a matching mechanism.
If the BaseTemplateBody on the right hand side of a modified template contains references to variables, the variables ARE evaluated before the modification.
An uninitialized field or element of a variable referenced in the BaseTemplateBody of a modified template IS treated as unspecified, i.e. as if specified with the not used symbol "-".
Modifications of a modified template ARE applied in a linked fashion, eventually tracing back to the original template.

For templates, template fields and list elements of simple types, union types and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template replaces the corresponding content of the parent template.

For templates, template fields and elements of record and set types, a field matching mechanism specified in the modified template replaces the matching mechanism of the corresponding field of the parent template.

If a record or set field is left unspecified in the modified template, implicitly or explicitly by the not used symbol "-", the matching mechanism of the corresponding field of the parent template SHALL be used.
When the field to be modified is nested within a structured template field, no other field of that structured field IS changed apart from the explicitly denoted one(s).
For templates, template fields and elements of record of and set of types, the modification rules for record and set types apply, with the deviations listed for record of and set of types.

If the value list notation is used in a modified template of record of or set of type, only the number of elements listed in the modified template IS inherited from the parent, i.e. the list is truncated at the last element of the list notation in the modified template.

When individual elements of a modified template or modified template field of record of or set of type are to be changed, the index assignment notation MAY be used, with the index of the element to be altered on the left hand side of the assignment.
The index assignment notation in a modified template SHALL only be used when individual elements of a record of or set of template or template field are to be changed.
For record of and set of types, rule (c) (e.g. truncation) IS applied first to the complete structure, and the further modification rules are then applied to the remaining individual elements.

A formal value or template parameter of a modified template inherits the default value or default template of the corresponding parameter of its parent template only if the dash (don't change) symbol is used in place of the default value or default template.
A modified template MAY have a template restriction.
A modified template, or a field of a modified record or set template, MAY be declared fuzzy using the `@fuzzy` modifier.
A modified field with the `@fuzzy` modifier becomes fuzzy even if it was not fuzzy in the base template, and IS evaluated as described for fuzzy fields in clause 6.2.1.0.

A modified field without the `@fuzzy` modifier that was marked `@fuzzy` in the base template loses fuzzy evaluation, and the template on the right hand side of its assignment SHALL be evaluated just once, when the assignment is evaluated for the first time.
If a fuzzy modified template modifies a non-fuzzy unparameterized template, the inherited fields before modification ARE the same for every evaluation of the fuzzy template.
A modified template SHALL NOT refer to itself, either directly or indirectly (recursive derivation).

A modified template derived (in one or several steps) from a base template with a formal parameter list SHALL NOT omit parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the modified template.

A modified template derived from a base template with a formal parameter list SHALL NOT change the types or names of parameters defined at any of the modification steps between the base template and the modified template.
A modified template MAY change the template parameter restriction of a formal parameter specified at any modification step between the base template and the modified template to a stricter one.
A modified template derived from a parameterized base template MAY have additional parameters appended to the formal parameter list.

If the dash (don't change) symbol is used in place of a default value or default template of a formal parameter of a modified template, the corresponding parameter of the parent template SHALL have a valid default value or default template, either assigned directly or inherited.
If the dash (don't change) symbol is used as default of a modified template parameter and the corresponding parent parameter has no valid default value or default template, this SHALL cause an error.
Referencing elements of templates or template fields in a modified template SHALL follow the rules for the left hand side of assignments given in clause 15.6.
A modified template SHALL obey the limitations on template restrictions described in clause 15.8.
A global or local modified template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL be completely initialized after its initialization is completed.
If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template derived from it SHALL have the same or a less strict template restriction (see table 13b).
If the base template does not have a template restriction, the modified template derived from it SHALL NOT have a template restriction.
The initialization of a modified template without parameters IS completed at the place of its declaration.
The initialization of a parameterized modified template IS completed at the time of its use.
The rules of clause 15.6 apply to referencing elements of templates or template fields of unrestricted templates or templates with the `present` restriction.
When referencing elements of templates or template fields with the `value` or `omit` restriction, the rules for referencing elements of values ARE used.
An individual string element inside a template or template field MAY be referenced only if at least one of the conditions listed in clause 15.6.1 is fulfilled.

An individual string element of a template of a character string type MAY be referenced if the template contains a specific value, a pattern or AnyValue, or, when the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment, AnyValueOrNone.
When indexing a character string template containing a pattern, each metacharacter described in clause B.1.5.0 IS treated as a single item for indexing purposes according to the rules of table B.1.
An individual string element of a template of a binary string type MAY be referenced if the template contains a specific value, a matching mechanism inside a value, AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone.
When indexing a binary string template, a matching mechanism inside a value IS treated as a single item for indexing purposes.
An individual string element of a template of a binary string type MAY be referenced if the template contains a combined template.

When an individual string element of a binary string template containing a combined template is referenced, the individual items of the combined template ARE concatenated and the reference IS applied to the result of the concatenation using the rules of clause 15.6.1.
A template whose individual string elements are referenced MAY contain the ifpresent and length matching attributes.

When a reference to an individual string element of a template occurs on the right hand side of an assignment, the result of the reference IS always a template with the content defined by rules a) to j) of clause 15.6.1.

When the referenced template is of a binary or character string type to which a specific value is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of items in the specific value, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing the single referenced element.

The specific value resulting from a right hand side reference to a string template element CAN contain either a single item of the string type (bit, hex, octet or character) or a matching mechanism inside a value such as AnyElement or AnyElementOrNone.

When the referenced template is of a character string type to which a pattern is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of characters and indexable metacharacters in the pattern, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing the single referenced character or metacharacter.
When the referenced template is of a binary string type to which AnyValue is assigned, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism.

When the referenced template is of a binary string type to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism with the ifpresent matching attribute attached.
When the referenced template is of a character string type and contains AnyValue, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing a single ? metacharacter.

When the referenced template is of a character string type and contains AnyValueOrNone, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing a single ? metacharacter with the ifpresent matching attribute attached.

If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute, a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL be resolved only if the index is less than the maximum allowed length.
The result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element of a template with a length matching attribute SHALL NOT contain the length matching attribute.
If the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute, the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL contain the ifpresent matching attribute as well.

If the referenced template has the present restriction, or the referenced field is unrestricted and represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL have the present restriction.
If the referenced template has the omit template restriction (value or omit), the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL have the value template restriction.

When a reference to an individual string element of a template occurs on the left hand side of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment SHALL contain either a string value, a specific value of a compatible type, or a pattern.

A string value or specific value on the right hand side of an assignment to an individual string element of a template SHALL contain exactly one indexable item (a bit, hex, octet, character or matching mechanism inside a value).

When an item of a binary string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the number of items in the specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.

When an item at index n of a binary string template containing a specific value is assigned and n is greater than or equal to the number of items in the specific value, AnyElement matching symbols SHALL first be appended to the specific value as many times as the difference between n and the number of items, and then the item from the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be appended.

When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.

When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using an index equal to the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the character from the right hand side SHALL be appended to the specific value.

When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index greater than the string length, or the right hand side is a pattern, the specific value SHALL be converted into a pattern that matches precisely the specific value, escaping characters with metacharacter meaning by a backslash.

After converting the specific value of a character string template into a pattern, the rules for referencing an item of a pattern on the left hand side of an assignment SHALL be applied to assign the right hand side to this pattern.
The pattern modified by an assignment to an item of a converted character string specific value IS assigned to the referenced template.

When an item of a character string template containing a pattern is assigned using a non-negative index less than the number of items in the pattern, the referenced character or metacharacter SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.

When an item at index n of a character string template containing a pattern is assigned and n is greater than or equal to the number of items in the pattern, ? metacharacters SHALL first be appended to the pattern as many times as the difference between n and the number of items, and then the item from the right hand side SHALL be appended to the pattern.

If the right hand side of an assignment to an item of a character string template (rules e), f) and g)) contains a pattern with more than one item, the pattern SHALL be implicitly converted into a single group metacharacter by enclosing it in parentheses before the assignment.

When an item of a binary string template containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone is assigned using a non-negative index, a binary string of length 0 IS assigned to the referenced template and rule b) IS applied to finish the assignment.
After an assignment to an item of a binary string template that contained AnyValueOrNone, the ifpresent matching attribute SHALL be added to the referenced template if it does not already contain it.

When an item of a character string template containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone is assigned using a non-negative index, a pattern of length 0 IS assigned to the referenced template and rule g) IS applied to finish the assignment.

After an assignment to an item of a character string template that contained AnyValueOrNone, the ifpresent matching attribute SHALL be added to the referenced template if it does not already contain it.

If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute and the index of a left hand side reference is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length, the maximum allowed length SHALL be changed to the index + 1.
The ifpresent matching attribute of the referenced template IS NOT removed by an assignment to an individual string element.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error for every reference to an individual string element of a template that is not covered by the rules of clause 15.6.1.

A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a template referenced by index notation (on either side of an assignment) contains a matching symbol other than those listed in clause 15.6.1, such as omit, a template list or a complemented template list.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index used to reference an individual string element of a template is negative.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index used on the right hand side of an assignment is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length of the referenced template.

A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index is used on the left hand side of an assignment and the right hand side contains a binary string value or specific template with not exactly one indexable item.
A template or template variable MAY reference a sub-field inside a template definition using the dot notation.
A field referenced by dot notation in a template CAN be a subfield of a structured field to which a matching mechanism is assigned.

Referencing, on the right hand side of an assignment, a subfield within a structured field to which omit, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented template list is assigned SHALL cause an error.
When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS implicitly set to be present.

When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
During the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValueOrNone or omit, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be assigned to optional subfields.
After the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValueOrNone or omit, the value or matching mechanism on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
Referencing, on the left hand side of an assignment, a subfield within a structured field to which a template list or a complemented template list is assigned SHALL cause an error.

When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment, AnyValue SHALL be returned for a mandatory subfield and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be returned for an optional subfield.

When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS implicitly expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
During the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValue, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be assigned to optional subfields.
After the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValue, the value or matching mechanism on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.

Referencing a subfield within a structured field to which the ifpresent matching attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended.
Referencing a field of an address type value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
A template or a template variable MAY reference an element of a record of, set of or array template or field using the index notation.
A matching mechanism CAN be assigned to the record of, set of or array template or field within which an element is referenced by the index notation.
Referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which `omit` is assigned SHALL follow the rules specified in clause 6.2.3.
Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a template list, a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.

When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue without a length attribute is assigned is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL return AnyValue.
If a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue assigned to a record of or set of template or field, the index of an element reference SHALL NOT violate the length attribute.

When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.

When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, AnyElement SHALL be assigned to all elements before the referenced element (if any).

When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, a single AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added at the end of the resulting template or field.

When a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue and an element is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the length attribute SHALL be conveyed transparently to the new template or field.
The index of an element reference into a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned SHALL NOT violate the type restrictions of the record of or set of type.
Referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone (with or without a length attribute) is assigned at the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.

When an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for AnyValue (item c) of clause 15.6.3) SHALL apply.
Referencing, by its index, an element of a record of template or field that is located inside a permutation SHALL cause an error.
The record of element indexes covered by a permutation SHALL be determined by the number of elements of the permutation.
A permutation that contains AnyElementsOrNone as a permutation element IS considered to cover all record of element indexes from its position onward.

Referencing an element within a record of or set of field to which the `ifpresent` attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which `ifpresent` is appended.

The result of referencing an element of a record of or set of template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone IS dependent on the position of AnyElementsOrNone, the referenced index and the length attributes attached to AnyElementsOrNone.
When a reference to an element of a record of or set of template containing AnyElementsOrNone is resolved, the transformed form of the template IS used.

The transformed form of a record of or set of template IS equal to the original template with every AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction replaced by a sequence of AnyElement symbols whose size is the lower bound of the length restriction.

If the upper bound of the length restriction of an AnyElementsOrNone is greater than its lower bound, the sequence of AnyElement symbols in the transformed form SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.

The length restriction of the AnyElementsOrNone appended in the transformed form IS a restriction with lower bound zero and upper bound equal to the difference between the upper and lower bound of the original restriction.
Referencing an element of an address type whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.

When an element reference is used at the right hand side of an assignment and the positions of all AnyElementsOrNone symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item, the reference IS resolved using the rules of clause 6.2.3.2.

When an element reference is used at the right hand side of an assignment and the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of any AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed template, the reference SHALL cause an error.

When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position and the referenced item is not a result of transformation, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL replace the referenced symbol in the original template.

When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position and the referenced item is a result of transformation, the AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the original template IS replaced with its transformed form and the assignment IS performed afterwards.

When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and that AnyElementsOrNone symbol is not the last element of the template, the reference SHALL cause an error.

When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and that AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol of the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.

After the assignment to an element at or beyond a trailing AnyElementsOrNone, the AnyElementsOrNone symbol and all unbound values between it and the referenced symbol SHALL be replaced with AnyElement symbols.
If the trailing AnyElementsOrNone symbol had a length restriction, the number of AnyElement symbols added in its place SHALL NOT exceed the upper bound of the length restriction.
As the last step of an assignment to an element at or beyond a trailing AnyElementsOrNone, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol CAN be appended to the end of the template.
If the original trailing AnyElementsOrNone symbol was unrestricted, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS always appended to the end of the template after the assignment.

If the original trailing AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS appended to the end of the template only if the restriction included items beyond the referenced item.
The appended AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS given the original length restriction adjusted by the difference between the size of the template before and after the assignment.
The index of an item referenced in a record of or set of template containing AnyElementsOrNone SHALL NOT violate the type restrictions of the record of or set of type.
A signature parameter of a signature template SHALL NOT be referenced directly (e.g. using dot notation), except when modifying the signature template.
A modified signature template MAY reference a signature parameter of its parent signature template.
A matching mechanism CAN be assigned to a signature template as a whole.
Referencing a signature parameter of a signature template to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

When a signature parameter of a signature template to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the signature template IS implicitly expanded to the parameter level.
During the implicit expansion of a signature template to which AnyValue is assigned, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to all signature parameters of the template.
After the implicit expansion of the signature template, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced signature parameter.
A template or a template variable MAY reference an alternative inside a union template using the dot notation.
A referenced union alternative CAN belong to a template field to which a matching mechanism is assigned.

Referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which `omit`, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the right hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field IS implicitly set to be present.

When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative IS made the chosen alternative.

If the referenced alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is not the last element of the dot notation, the rules of clause 15.6.2 for AnyValue SHALL apply recursively for further expansion.

After the expansion of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL return AnyValue.

When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative IS made the chosen alternative.

If the referenced alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned is not the last element of the dot notation, the rules of clause 15.6.2 for AnyValue SHALL apply recursively for further expansion.

After the expansion of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.

Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which the `ifpresent` attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which `ifpresent` is appended.
Referencing an alternative of an address type whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
A template or a template variable MAY reference an element of a map template or field using the index notation.
A matching mechanism CAN be assigned to the map template or field within which an element is referenced.
Referencing an element within a map template or field to which `omit` is assigned SHALL follow the rules specified in clause 6.2.15.7.
Referencing an element within a map template or field to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned SHALL cause an error.
When an element of a map template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL return AnyValueOrNone.

When an element of a map template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the template or field IS implicitly expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.

When an element of a map template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, AnyValue IS assigned to the referenced field during the implicit expansion.

After the implicit expansion of a map template or field to which AnyValue is assigned, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced field.
After the assignment to an element of a map template or field to which AnyValue was assigned, AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added to the map template.
Referencing an element within a map template or field to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned at the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
When an element within a map template or field to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for AnyValue (item c) of clause 15.6.6) SHALL apply.

Referencing an element within a map template or field to which the `ifpresent` attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which `ifpresent` is appended.

When an element of a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced element is not present, the reference SHALL return AnyValueOrNone.

When an element that is not present is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment in a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, the template or field IS implicitly expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.

When an element that is not present is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment in a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, AnyValue IS assigned to the referenced field during the implicit expansion.

After the implicit expansion of a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced field.
After the assignment to a non-present element of a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added to the map template.
Referencing an element of an address type that is derived from a map type and whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
A matching mechanism MAY be used to replace the value of a single template field.
A matching mechanism MAY be used to replace the entire contents of a template.
A matching mechanism MAY be used in-line, i.e. in an in-line template.

A matching mechanism IS classified into one of four groups: specific values, special symbols that can be used instead of values, special symbols that can be used inside values, and special symbols which describe attributes of values.
Certain matching mechanisms MAY be used in combination with each other.
A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be applied to a value or template of a type for which table 11 does not allow it.
`omit` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
`ifpresent` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
When matching, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
When matching, AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
When matching, `ifpresent` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
For character string types, AnyElement (`?`) and AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) IS a matching mechanism only within a character pattern.
A specific value IS the basic matching mechanism of TTCN-3 templates.
A specific value in a template IS an expression that does not contain any matching mechanism.
A specific value matching mechanism has the syntax SingleExpression.
The specific value matching mechanism IS an expression that evaluates to a specific value.

A template or template field of a `boolean` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `integer` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Range and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `float` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Range and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `bitstring` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `octetstring` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `hexstring` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a character string type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), Range, Pattern, Match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement (`?`) (subject to NOTE 2), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 2), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `record` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `record of` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), Permutation, LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of an array MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1), AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), Permutation, LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `set` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `set of` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`), Superset, Subset, AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `enumerated` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `union` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).

A template or template field of a `anytype` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`) (subject to NOTE 1) and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).
A matching mechanism of the group of special symbols that can be used instead of values characterizes a set of values.

A special symbol used instead of values has one of the syntaxes: `omit`; a template list "(" {TemplateInstance | all from TemplateInstance [","]} ")"; `complement` "(" {TemplateInstance | all from TemplateInstance [","]} ")"; "?"; "*"; a range "(" (ConstantExpression | -infinity) ".." (ConstantExpression | infinity) ")"; `superset` "(" ... ")"; `subset` "(" ... ")"; `pattern` [@nocase] Cstring; `decmatch` ["(" Expression ")"] TemplateInstance; or EnumValueIdentifier "(" TemplateBody {"," TemplateBody} ")".
The `omit` matching mechanism matches if the optional field in which it is used is not present.
`omit` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
`omit` CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
The template list matching mechanism `(…)` IS a list of values or templates.
The `complement (…)` matching mechanism IS the complement of a list of values or templates.
The AnyValue matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any value.
The AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any value or no value at all, i.e. a field that is not present.
AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
The range matching mechanism `(lowerBound .. upperBound)` matches integer or float values between and including the lower bound and the upper bound.
The `superset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at least all of the listed elements, and possibly more.
The `subset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at most the listed elements, and possibly fewer.
The `pattern` matching mechanism matches a charstring or universal charstring value that matches the given format.
The `decmatch` matching mechanism IS used for matching encoded payload fields.
An EnumValueIdentifier with a list of templates IS used for matching enumerated values with an associated value list.
The template list, complemented list, `subset` and `superset` matching mechanisms MAY use the elements of a template by means of the `all from` clause.
Every template and value used in a matching mechanism used instead of values, including referenced ones such as those within a pattern, SHALL be completely initialized.
A matching mechanism of the group of special symbols that can be used inside values characterizes a value set by varying values inside a value.
A template containing a matching mechanism inside a value notation IS called a combined template.
A special symbol used inside values has one of the syntaxes "?", "*" or `permutation` "(" {(TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance) [","]} ")", each appearing inside a value notation.
The AnyElement matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any single element in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value.
The AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any number of consecutive elements in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value, or no element at all.
The `permutation` matching mechanism matches all of the listed elements in an arbitrary order.
AnyElement (`?`) and AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) MAY be used as elements of a permutation list.
All elements of a template MAY be added to a `permutation` by means of the `all from` clause.
Every template or value used in a `permutation` matching mechanism SHALL be completely initialized.
A matching mechanism of the group of special symbols which describe attributes of values defines properties of values.
An attribute matching mechanism has the syntax `length` "(" ConstantExpression [".." (ConstantExpression | infinity)] ")" [`ifpresent`], or `ifpresent` alone.
The `length` matching attribute restricts the string length of a value of a string type and the number of elements of a `record of`, `set of` or array value.
The `ifpresent` matching attribute matches an optional field that is omitted, and applies the matching of the template it is attached to when the optional field is present.
`ifpresent` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
`ifpresent` CAN be used for matching optional fields only.

Assigning `ifpresent` to a template that already matches `omit` (i.e. `omit`, an `ifpresent` template or AnyValueOrNone) has no effect, and the resulting template matches the same set of values and `omit` as the original template.
Every value used in a `length` matching attribute SHALL be completely initialized.
A template restriction IS a restriction of the matching mechanisms that MAY be used with a template.
A template restriction MAY be applied to template definitions, template variables, formal template parameters and return template types of functions.
A template restriction MAY be applied equally to message templates and signature templates.
A restricted template type has the syntax `template` "(" ( `omit` | `present` | `value` ) ")" Type.
A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
Each field of a template with the `omit` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
A template with the `omit` restriction MAY resolve to `omit` as a whole.
A template with the `omit` restriction CAN be used to define a field of a record or set template.
A record or set template whose field is defined by a template with the `omit` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
A template with the `value` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value.
Each field of a template with the `value` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
A template with the `value` restriction SHALL NOT resolve to `omit` as a whole.
A template with the `value` restriction CAN be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template.
A record or set template whose mandatory field is defined by a template with the `value` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
A template with the `present` restriction SHALL NOT resolve as a whole to a matching mechanism that matches `omit`.
A field of a template with the `present` restriction MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute.
A template with the `present` restriction CAN be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template.
A template restriction allows a TTCN-3 tool to check more easily at compile time whether templates and matching expressions are used correctly.
Whether a TTCN-3 tool checks template restrictions at compile time (rejecting invalid code) or at execution time (raising dynamic errors) IS outside the scope of the present document.
A matching mechanism SHALL be used within a restricted template only as permitted by table 12.
A restricted or unrestricted template SHALL be used as actual parameter of a formal template parameter, or assigned to a template or template variable, only as permitted by table 13.
A formal template parameter of a modified template MAY have a stricter restriction than the same formal parameter of the base template, as permitted by table 13a.
A modified template MAY have a less strict restriction than its base template, as permitted by table 13b.
A template with the `omit` restriction MAY use the SpecificValue matching mechanism.
A template with the `omit` restriction MAY use the Omit matching mechanism.

A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL NOT use the matching mechanisms ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue, AnyValueOrNone, Range, Superset, Subset, Pattern, match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement, AnyElementsOrNone, Permutation, LengthRestriction or IfPresent.
A template with the `value` restriction MAY use the SpecificValue matching mechanism.
A field of a template with the `value` restriction MAY use the Omit matching mechanism.
A template with the `value` restriction SHALL NOT resolve as a whole to the Omit matching mechanism.

A template with the `value` restriction SHALL NOT use the matching mechanisms ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue, AnyValueOrNone, Range, Superset, Subset, Pattern, match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement, AnyElementsOrNone, Permutation, LengthRestriction or IfPresent.

A template with the `present` restriction MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue, Range, Superset, Subset, Pattern, AnyElement, AnyElementsOrNone, Permutation and LengthRestriction.
A field of a template with the `present` restriction MAY use the Omit and AnyValueOrNone matching mechanisms and the IfPresent attribute.
A template with the `present` restriction SHALL NOT resolve as a whole to the Omit or AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism or to a template with the IfPresent attribute.
A template with the `present` restriction MAY use the match decoded content (`decmatch`) matching mechanism only if the template following the `decmatch` keyword fulfils the `present` restriction.
Where table 12 refers to NOTE 1, a matching mechanism MAY be used in fields of the restricted template, but the template as a whole SHALL NOT resolve to that matching mechanism.
Where table 12 refers to NOTE 2, the match decoded content (`decmatch`) matching mechanism IS allowed only if the template following the `decmatch` keyword fulfils the given template restriction.

A value, a template with the `omit` restriction or a template with the `value` restriction MAY be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `omit` restriction.

A template with the `present` restriction or an unrestricted template SHALL NOT be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `omit` restriction.

A value or a template with the `value` restriction MAY be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `value` restriction.

A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL NOT be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `value` restriction, except as permitted by the rule of table 13.

A template with the `present` restriction or an unrestricted template SHALL NOT be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `value` restriction.

A value, a template with the `value` restriction or a template with the `present` restriction MAY be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `present` restriction.

A template with the `omit` restriction or an unrestricted template SHALL NOT be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for a formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment with the `present` restriction.

A value, a restricted template of any restriction or an unrestricted template MAY be used as actual parameter or right hand side of an assignment for an unrestricted formal template parameter or left hand side of an assignment.
A template with the `omit` restriction MAY be used on the right hand side of an assignment if the left hand side resolves into an optional field of a template with the `value` restriction.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `omit` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template MAY have the `omit` or the `value` restriction.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `omit` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template SHALL NOT have the `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `value` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template MAY have the `value` restriction.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `value` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit` or `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `present` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template MAY have the `value` or the `present` restriction.
If the formal parameter of the base template has the `present` restriction, a formal template parameter of a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the formal parameter of the base template is unrestricted, a formal template parameter of a modified template MAY have any template restriction or be unrestricted.
A template field, alternative or element referenced using dot notation, index notation or template modification SHALL have an implicit template restriction as given in table 13c.
All rules of clause 15.8.1 for templates with an explicit restriction SHALL apply equally to template fields, alternatives and elements with an implicit restriction.
If the base template has the `omit` restriction, a modified template MAY have the `omit` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the base template has the `omit` restriction, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `value` or `present` restriction.
If the base template has the `value` restriction, a modified template MAY have the `omit`, `value` or `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the base template has the `present` restriction, a modified template MAY have the `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
If the base template has the `present` restriction, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit` or `value` restriction.
If the base template is unrestricted, a modified template MAY be unrestricted.
If the base template is unrestricted, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit`, `value` or `present` restriction.

A mandatory field of a record or set template, an alternative of a union or anytype template, or an element of a record of, set of, array, map or the parameters of a signature template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(value)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `omit` or `value` restriction.

A mandatory field of a record or set template, an alternative of a union or anytype template, or an element of a record of, set of, array, map or the parameters of a signature template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(present)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted.
An optional field of a record or set template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(omit)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `omit` or `value` restriction.
An optional field of a record or set template SHALL be implicitly unrestricted if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted.
The `match` operation IS the operation that compares a value, specified as an expression, with a template.
The `match` operation has the syntax `match` "(" Expression "," TemplateInstance ")".
The `match` operation returns a `boolean` value.
The expression parameter of the `match` operation SHALL denote a value or a field of a value.
The type of the expression parameter and the type of the template instance parameter of the `match` operation SHALL be compatible.
The `match` operation returns `true` if the expression matches the template instance and `false` otherwise.
A non-optional value expression MAY be matched with a template instance that matches an omitted field (Omit, AnyValueOrNone or IfPresent).
When a non-optional value expression is matched with a template instance that matches an omitted field, the `match` operation SHALL treat the value expression as if it were a present optional field.
The `match` operation SHALL return `false` when a value expression is matched against a template instance that evaluates to the Omit matching mechanism.
The expression parameter of the `match` operation SHALL evaluate to a value or denote an omitted optional field.
The `match` operation SHALL NOT be used to compare two templates.
The operands of the `match` operation SHALL be completely initialized.
The type of the template instance parameter of the `match` operation SHALL be unambiguously identified.

If the expression parameter of the `match` operation evaluates to a literal value without explicit or implicit identification of its type, the type of the template instance parameter SHALL be used as the type context of the expression parameter.
The `valueof` operation IS the operation that returns the value specified within a template.
The value returned by the `valueof` operation MAY be assigned to a variable, used in an expression or used as an actual value parameter.
The `valueof` operation has the syntax `valueof` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
The `valueof` operation returns the value of its template instance parameter.
The template instance parameter of the `valueof` operation SHALL be completely initialized.
The template instance parameter of the `valueof` operation SHALL resolve to a specific value.

A template of a string type or list type (`bitstring`, `octetstring`, `hexstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of`, `set of` or array) MAY be concatenated from several single in-line templates using the concatenation operation.
Each single template of a template concatenation, except for templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` types, SHALL have the same root type.

A single template of a binary string type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, a combined template, AnyValue without a length modifier, or AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone constrained to a fixed length.
The concatenation of templates of binary string types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
When concatenating templates of binary string types, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier SHALL be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation.

When concatenating templates of binary string types, an AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol constrained to a fixed length N SHALL be replaced by N AnyElement matching symbols before concatenation.

A single template of a list type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, a combined template, AnyValue with or without a length modifier, or AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier.
The concatenation of templates of list types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
When concatenating templates of list types, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier SHALL be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation.

When concatenating templates of list types, an AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol with a length modifier SHALL be replaced by an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism with the same length modifier before concatenation.

A single template of `charstring` or `universal charstring` type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, AnyValue with or without a length modifier, AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier, or a pattern.
When concatenating templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` types, each single template SHALL be of the `charstring` or the `universal charstring` type.

When templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` type are both present in a concatenation, each `charstring` value IS implicitly converted to a `universal charstring` value according to clause 6.3.1 before concatenation.
When templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` type are both present in a concatenation, the resulting template IS of the `universal charstring` type.
The concatenation of templates of character string types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
If all operands of a character string template concatenation are specific values, the result of the concatenation IS a specific value.
If not all operands of a character string template concatenation are specific values, the result of the concatenation IS a pattern, if possible.
When producing a pattern from a character string template concatenation, each single template IS first transformed to a character string according to table 14.
When producing a pattern from a character string template concatenation, the pattern IS created from the concatenation of the transformed strings.
If one of the single templates of a character string template concatenation is a pattern with the `@nocase` modifier, all other single templates SHALL also be patterns with the `@nocase` modifier.
If one of the single templates of a character string template concatenation is a pattern with the `@nocase` modifier, the resulting pattern IS also with the `@nocase` modifier.
Concatenation of character strings in a pattern definition IS taking precedence over concatenation of templates.
If a pattern definition is to be concatenated with a following character string according to the template concatenation rules, the pattern definition SHALL be enclosed in parentheses.
A template concatenation SHALL be performed completely before the resulting template is used (e.g. for assignment or matching).
The template resulting from a template concatenation SHALL be type-compatible with the place of its use.
A length matching attribute SHALL NOT directly follow a template or template field produced by concatenation.
If a length matching attribute is applied to a template or template field produced by concatenation, the concatenation SHALL be placed within a pair of parentheses.
The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to template concatenation in addition to the restrictions of clause 15.11.
Every operand of the concatenation operation SHALL be at least partially initialized.

A specific value operand (character string) of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the character string escaped by inserting the "\" character before each of the characters "#", "(", ")", "*", "+", "-", "?", "[", "\", "]", "^", "{", "|", "}".
An operand `?`, `? length(0..infinity)` or `* length(0..infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "*".
An operand `? length(0)` or `* length(0)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the empty string.
An operand `? length(1)` or `* length(1)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?".
An operand `? length(1 .. infinity)` or `* length(1 .. infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?+".
An operand `? length(n)` or `* length(n)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n)".
An operand `? length(n .. infinity)` or `* length(n .. infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n,)".
An operand `? length(n .. m)` or `* length(n .. m)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n,m)".
An operand `pattern "content"` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "content".
The `omit` operation IS an operation that checks whether a template instance fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction.
The `omit` operation has the syntax `omit` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
If the operand fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction (clause 15.8), the `omit` operation IS returning a template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand.
If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the omit template restriction, the `omit` operation SHALL cause an error.
The result of the `omit` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the omit restriction.
The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to the `omit` operation.
The `present` operation IS an operation that checks whether a template instance fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction.
The `present` operation has the syntax `present` "(" TemplateInstance ")".

If the operand fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction (clause 15.8), the `present` operation IS returning a template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand.
If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the present template restriction, the `present` operation SHALL cause an error.
The result of the `present` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the present restriction.
The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to the `present` operation.
The presentness conversion IS the application of the `.present` notation to a general (unrestricted) template, converting it to a template with the present restriction.
The presentness conversion has the syntax TemplateInstance "." `present`.
Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no template restriction IS yielding a template with the present restriction.
If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion contains AnyValueOrNone, the presentness conversion IS yielding AnyValue.

If the matching mechanism of the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion has the `ifpresent` attribute attached, the presentness conversion IS yielding the same matching mechanism without the `ifpresent` attribute.

If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion is a template list, the presentness conversion IS yielding the template list with all alternatives that evaluate to `omit` removed and with the presentness conversion applied to all other alternatives.
In all cases other than AnyValueOrNone, a matching mechanism with `ifpresent` and a template list, the presentness conversion of an unrestricted template IS yielding the unchanged template.
A matching attribute other than `ifpresent`, such as a length restriction, IS NOT affected by the presentness conversion (e.g. `* length(2..10)` is converted to `? length(2..10)`).
Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the present or value restriction IS yielding the same template with the same template restriction.
Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction IS yielding the same template with the value restriction.
Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value `omit` SHALL result in an error.
