Every ValueRef in the `sender` clause of a `receive` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port.
No AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `receive` operation SHALL contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
The PortArrayRef of an `any from` `receive` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

The `call` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that invokes a procedure call.

The `call` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `call` "(" TemplateInstance [ "," ( CallTimerValue | `nowait` ) ] ")" [ `to` Address ].

The `call` operation IS used to specify that a test component calls a procedure in the SUT or in another test component.

The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation defines a set of alternatives describing the possible responses and exceptions to the call.

The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation IS executed like an `alt` statement without any active default.

The procedure-based communication operation "Invoke procedure call" IS denoted by the keyword `call`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Accept procedure call from remote entity" IS denoted by the keyword `getcall`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Reply to procedure call from remote entity" IS denoted by the keyword `reply`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Raise exception (to an accepted call)" IS denoted by the keyword `raise`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Handle response from a previous call" IS denoted by the keyword `getreply`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Catch exception (from called entity)" IS denoted by the keyword `catch`.
The procedure-based communication operation "Check call/exception/reply received" IS denoted by the keyword `check`.

A blocking procedure MAY have no return value, no out and inout parameters and raise no exception.
A `call` operation of a blocking procedure without return value, out parameters, inout parameters and exceptions SHALL have a response and exception handling part.
A non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT have out parameters, inout parameters or a return value.
The non-blocking property of a procedure IS indicated in its signature definition by the `noblock` keyword.
An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
The `call` operation supports unicast, multicast and broadcast calls of procedures, like the `send` operation.
For a unicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the address of one receiving entity.
For a multicast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS a list of addresses of a set of receivers.
For a broadcast call, the argument of the `to` clause of a `call` operation IS the `all component` keyword.
In case of a one-to-one connection, the `to` clause of a `call` operation MAY be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.
A multicast or broadcast `call` operation CAN cause several responses and exceptions from different communication partners.

The assignment of the procedure return value and of out and inout parameter values to variables SHALL be made explicitly in the response and exception handling part of the `call` operation by `getreply` and `catch` operations.

A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT have a response and exception handling part.

The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
If the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type, the encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.

A `getcall` on any port from a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.

For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getcall` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.

The `getcall` operation SHALL only be used on procedure-based ports.

The ParameterIdentifiers in the `param` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be from the corresponding signature definition.
The value assignment part (`-> value`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.

Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.

Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.
An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.

The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `stop`.
The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `read`.
The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `running`.
The timer operation 'Overview of TTCN-3 timer operations' IS denoted by the keyword `timeout`.
Each test component and each control component SHALL maintain its own running-timer list (the list of all running timers) and its own timeout-list (the list of all timers that have timed out).
The timeout-list IS part of the snapshot taken during the execution of a testcase.
The running-timer list and the timeout-list of a component ARE updated when a timer of the component is started, is stopped or times out, or when the component executes a timeout operation.

A TTCN-3 tool MAY implement the running-timer list and the timeout-list with other data structures, such as a set in which access to timeout events is not restricted by the order of the timeout events.
Each test component and control component conceptually maintains exactly one running-timer list and one timeout-list.
Within a scope unit, only timers known in the scope unit (declared in it, passed in as parameters, or known via a runs on clause) CAN be accessed individually.
Stopping timers local to other scope units, or checking whether such timers are running or have timed out, CAN be necessary in special cases, e.g. when re-establishing a test component.
The keywords `all` and `any` CAN be combined with the timer operations `stop`, `timeout` and `running` to address timers local to other scope units.
When a timer expires, the timer IS immediately inactive.
When a timer expires, a timeout event IS placed in the timeout-list of the component for which the timer has been declared.
When a timer expires, the timer IS removed from the running-timer list of the component for which the timer has been declared.
The timeout-list of the component for which a timer has been declared SHALL NOT contain more than one entry for that timer.
The running-timer list of the component for which a timer has been declared SHALL NOT contain more than one entry for that timer.
All running timers of a test component SHALL be cancelled automatically when the test component is explicitly or implicitly stopped.
The start timer operation IS used to indicate that a timer shall start running.
The start timer operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." start [ "(" TimerValue ")" ].
When a timer is started, the timer IS added to the running-timer list.
The start timer operation SHALL specify a timer value if the timer declaration gives no default duration.
The start timer operation MAY specify a timer value to override the default duration given in the timer declaration.
A timer value given in a start timer operation IS applied only to the current instance of the timer.
A later start timer operation that does not specify a timer value SHALL use the default duration of the timer.
A timer started with the timer value 0.0 times out immediately.
Starting a timer with a negative timer value (e.g. resulting from an expression) SHALL cause a runtime error.
Starting a timer without a specified timer value SHALL cause a runtime error when the timer has no default duration.
The timer clock IS running from the float value 0.0 up to the maximum given by the duration.
The start timer operation MAY be applied to a running timer.
When the start timer operation is applied to a running timer, the timer IS stopped and re-started.
The start timer operation MAY be applied to a timer that has already expired.
When the start timer operation is applied to an expired timer, any entry for the timer in the timeout-list SHALL be removed.
The SingleExpression giving the timer value of a start timer operation SHALL be a non-negative float value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
The timer value of a start timer operation SHALL NOT be `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
The ObjectReference of a start timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
The stop timer operation IS used to stop a running timer.
The stop timer operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all timer ) "." stop.
A timer stopped by the stop timer operation IS removed from the running-timer list.
A stopped timer IS inactive.
The elapsed time of a stopped timer IS set to the float value 0.0.
Stopping an inactive timer IS a valid operation without any effect.
When an expired timer is stopped, the entry for the timer IS removed from the timeout-list.
The `all` keyword MAY be used with the stop timer operation (`all timer.stop`) to stop all timers started on a test component or control component.
The ObjectReference of a stop timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
The read timer operation IS used to retrieve the time elapsed since the specified timer was started.
The read timer operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." read.
The result of the read timer operation IS the time elapsed since the specified timer was started.
The value returned by the read timer operation SHALL be of type float.
When applied to an inactive timer (a timer not in the running-timer list), the result of the read timer operation IS the float value 0.0.
The ObjectReference of a read timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
The running timer operation IS used to check whether a timer is in the running-timer list.
The running timer operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." running [ "->" @index value ValueRef ].
The running timer operation IS checking whether a specific timer visible in the scope unit is in the running-timer list, i.e. has been started and has neither timed out nor been stopped.
The running timer operation IS returning `true` if the timer is in the running-timer list and `false` otherwise.
The `any` keyword MAY be used with the running timer operation (`any timer.running`) to check whether any timer started on a test component or control component is running.
The TimerArrayRef in an `any from` running timer operation SHALL be a timer array identifier.

In an `any from` running timer operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.
When a timer of the timer array is found in the running state, the result of an `any from` running timer operation IS `true` and the iteration stops.
If no timer of the timer array is running, the result of an `any from` running timer operation IS `false`.

The index of the first running timer found by an `any from` running timer operation MAY be stored via index redirection in an integer variable for a single-dimensional timer array, or in an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional timer array.
The TimerArrayRef of an `any from` running timer operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
The index redirection in a running timer operation SHALL only be used with an `any from` timer array running operation.
If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a single-dimensional timer array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the timer array.

If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.

If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
The ObjectReference of a running timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
The timeout operation IS used to check the expiration of timers.
The timeout operation has the syntax [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." timeout [ "->" @index value ValueRef ].

The timeout operation IS checking the expiration of a specific timer of the scope unit in which it is called, or of any timer started on the test component or control component before entering that scope.
When a timeout operation with a timer name is processed, the timeout-list IS searched according to the TTCN-3 scope rules.
If the timeout-list contains a timeout event matching the timer name, the event IS removed from the timeout-list and the timeout operation succeeds.
The timeout operation MAY be used as an alternative of an alt statement or as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
A stand-alone timeout operation IS shorthand for an alt statement with the timeout operation as its only alternative.
If the `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone timeout operation, the implicit alt statement IS an alt statement with the `@nodefault` modifier.
A timeout operation with the `any` keyword (`any timer.timeout`) IS successful if the timeout-list is not empty.
When a timeout operation with the `any` keyword succeeds, a randomly chosen timeout event IS removed from the timeout-list.
The TimerArrayRef in an `any from` timeout operation SHALL be a timer array identifier.

In an `any from` timeout operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually for timeout, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.
In an `any from` timeout operation, the first timer of the array found in the timeout-list IS removed from the timeout-list and the timeout operation succeeds.

The index of the matched timer of an `any from` timeout operation MAY be stored via index redirection in an integer variable for a single-dimensional timer array, or in an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional timer array.
The timeout operation IS NOT returning any value.
The timeout operation SHALL NOT be used in an expression.
The TimerArrayRef of an `any from` timeout operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
The index redirection in a timeout operation SHALL only be used with an `any from` timer array timeout operation.
If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a single-dimensional timer array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the timer array.

If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.

If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
The ObjectReference of a timeout operation SHALL be of the timer type.
The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in a stand-alone timeout statement.
The keywords `any` and `all` MAY be used with timer operations only as indicated in table 28.
A test verdict operation (`setverdict`, `getverdict`) IS an operation to set or retrieve a verdict.
A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions.
Each test component of the active configuration SHALL maintain its own local verdict.
A local verdict IS an entity owned by a single test component.
A local verdict IS created for each test component at the time of the creation of the test component.
The local verdict IS used to track the individual verdict of each test component, i.e. of the MTC and of every PTC.
The test system IS instantiating and handling a global test case verdict.
The test case verdict IS updated when a test component (the MTC or any PTC) terminates execution.
The test case verdict IS NOT accessible to the `getverdict` and `setverdict` operations.
When a testcase terminates execution, the testcase SHALL return the value of the test case verdict.
If the verdict returned by a testcase is not explicitly saved in the control component (e.g. assigned to a variable), then the returned verdict IS lost.
The keywords `any` and `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `start` operation.
The keyword `all` MAY be used with the timer `stop` operation (e.g. `all timer.stop`).
The keyword `any` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `stop` operation.
The keywords `any` and `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `read` operation.
The keyword `any` MAY be used with the timer `running` operation (e.g. `any timer.running`).
The keyword `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `running` operation.
The keyword `any` MAY be used with the timer `timeout` operation (e.g. `any timer.timeout`).
The keyword `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `timeout` operation.
The `setverdict` operation IS the statement that sets the local verdict.
The `getverdict` operation IS the statement that gets the local verdict.
The TTCN-3 language IS NOT specifying the actual mechanisms that update the local verdicts and the test case verdict.
The mechanisms that update the local verdicts and the test case verdict ARE implementation dependent.
A verdict IS one of the five distinguished values of `verdicttype`: `pass`, `fail`, `inconc`, `none` and `error`.
The verdict value `inconc` IS an inconclusive verdict.
When a test component is instantiated, the local verdict of the test component IS created.
When a test component is instantiated, the local verdict of the test component IS initialized to `none`.
When the value of the local verdict is changed with the `setverdict` operation, the effect of the change SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
The test case verdict IS implicitly updated on the termination of a test component.
The implicit update of the test case verdict on the termination of a test component SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
If the current verdict is `none`, assigning `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `none` IS resulting in the assigned value.
If the current verdict is `pass`, assigning `pass` or `none` IS resulting in `pass`, assigning `inconc` IS resulting in `inconc`, and assigning `fail` IS resulting in `fail`.
If the current verdict is `inconc`, assigning `pass`, `inconc` or `none` IS resulting in `inconc`, and assigning `fail` IS resulting in `fail`.
If the current verdict is `fail`, assigning any of `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `none` IS resulting in `fail`.
The `error` verdict IS set by the test system to indicate that a test case error (runtime error) has occurred.
The `setverdict` operation SHALL NOT set the `error` verdict.
The `getverdict` operation IS NOT returning the `error` verdict.
A verdict value other than `error` CANNOT override an `error` verdict.
An `error` verdict IS only obtainable as the result of an `execute` operation.
Each test component SHALL maintain, together with its local verdict, an implicit charstring variable storing information about the reasons for assigning the verdict.
The implicit charstring variable SHALL NOT have any effect on the verdict overwriting rules.
The implicit charstring variable SHALL NOT have any effect on the calculation of the final test case verdict.
On the termination of a test component, the local verdict of the test component SHALL be logged together with the implicit charstring variable.
The implicit charstring variable CANNOT be retrieved or read by any TTCN-3 language construct.
The implicit charstring variable IS only providing additional information for logging.
The local verdict IS set with the `setverdict` operation.

The `setverdict` operation has the syntax `setverdict ( SingleExpression { , ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) } )`, i.e. a verdict expression followed by zero or more free text or template instance arguments.
The `setverdict` operation IS changing the value of the local verdict.
The change of the local verdict by the `setverdict` operation SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
A `setverdict` operation MAY have optional FreeText or TemplateInstance arguments providing information that explains the reasons for assigning the verdict.
The information given in the optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation IS composed into a single string.
The string composed from the optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation IS stored in the implicit charstring variable of the test component.
On termination of a test component, the actual local verdict IS logged together with the implicit charstring variable.
The optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation SHALL obey the same rules and restrictions as the parameters of the `log` statement.
Whenever a `setverdict` operation overwrites the local verdict of a test component with a value different from the previous one, the implicit charstring variable IS overwritten.
If a `setverdict` operation does not change the value of the local verdict, the implicit charstring variable IS NOT overwritten.
A `setverdict` operation with only a verdict argument that overwrites the current local verdict IS clearing the implicit charstring variable, so that previously stored information is lost.
The `setverdict` operation SHALL only be used with the values `pass`, `fail`, `inconc` and `none`.
The `setverdict` operation SHALL NOT be used to assign the value `error`.
The `error` verdict IS set only by the test system to indicate runtime errors.
The SingleExpression of a `setverdict` operation SHALL resolve to a value of type `verdicttype`.
The FreeText and TemplateInstance arguments of a `setverdict` operation SHALL obey the same rules and restrictions as the parameters of the `log` statement.
The value of the local verdict MAY be retrieved using the `getverdict` operation.
The `getverdict` operation has the syntax `getverdict` (the keyword alone, without parentheses or arguments).
The `getverdict` operation IS returning the actual value of the local verdict as a `verdicttype` value.
The `action` statement provides the means to write one or more items, e.g. to a displaying device.
An item to be displayed by the `action` statement SHALL be identified in a comma-separated list in the argument of the `action` statement.
An item of the `action` statement MAY be an individual language element specified in table 18 or an expression composed of such items.
The `action` statement has the syntax `action` "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")".
The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions and altsteps.
The TTCN-3 language does not specify what is done to or by the SUT to trigger the external action; the `action` statement IS only an informal description of the required action.
A test case IS defined in the module definitions part.
The module control function IS the place that manages the execution of test cases.
An assignment (`:=`) MAY be used in control behaviour.
The if-else statement (`if (…) {…} else {…}`) MAY be used in control behaviour.
The select case statement (`select case`) MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `for` loop statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `while` loop statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `do`-`while` loop statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `label` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `goto` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `stop` statement (stop execution) MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `break` statement (leaving a loop, alt or interleave) MAY be used in control behaviour.
A test case IS executed by an `execute` statement in the module control function.
The `execute` statement has the syntax `execute ( TestcaseRef ( [ActualPar {, ActualPar}] ) [, TimerValue [, HostId]] )`.
The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case in control behaviour.
The result of an `execute` statement IS always a value of type `verdicttype`.
A test case SHALL contain exactly one MTC.
The MTC of a test case IS of the component type referenced in the header (`runs on` clause) of the test case definition.
The behaviour defined in the test case body IS the behaviour of the MTC.
When a test case is invoked, the MTC IS created.
When a test case is invoked, the ports of the MTC and of the test system interface ARE instantiated.
When a test case is invoked, the behaviour specified in the test case definition IS started on the MTC.

The TTCN-3 tool SHALL create the MTC, instantiate the ports of the MTC and the test system interface, and start the test case behaviour on the MTC implicitly, without explicit `create` and `start` operations.
The `execute` statement SHALL return a test case verdict of `none`, `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `error` as the result of the execution of the test case.
The verdict returned by an `execute` statement MAY be assigned to a variable.
An `execute` statement MAY specify a timer duration (TimerValue) to supervise the execution of the test case.
An `execute` statement MAY specify a host to which the MTC is deployed before the execution of the test case starts.
The host for MTC deployment in an `execute` statement IS identified by a host id.
A variable visible in the scope unit of an `execute` statement SHALL be passed to the test case as an actual parameter if it is to be used in the behaviour definition of that test case.
The TTCN-3 language does NOT support global variables of any kind.
The test configuration SHALL be reset at the start of each test case.

A test component or port created or connected (by `create`, `connect`, etc. operations) in a previous test case IS destroyed when that test case is stopped and IS NOT visible to a subsequent test case.
A test case terminates when its MTC terminates.
When the MTC terminates (explicitly or implicitly), the test system SHALL remove all running PTCs.
The `continue` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `log` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `alt` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
The `repeat` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
The `interleave` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
The `activate` operation MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
The `deactivate` operation MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
The timer `start` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
The timer `stop` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
The timer `read` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
The timer `running` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
The timer `timeout` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `action` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The `execute` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
The concrete mechanism for stopping all PTCs at MTC termination IS tool specific and outside the scope of the standard.
The final verdict of a test case IS calculated from the final local verdicts of the test components according to the rules of clause 24.1.
The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, by another test component or by the test system.
The MTC SHOULD ensure, by means of the `done` or `killed` operation, that all PTCs have stopped before it stops itself.
The execution of a test case MAY be supervised by a timer.
Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the result of the `execute` statement SHALL be the verdict `error`.
If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the test system SHALL terminate the test case.
The timer used for test case supervision IS a system timer.
The test case supervision timer NEED NOT be declared or started.
If a host id is given in an `execute` statement, the MTC SHALL be started and execute its behaviour on the deployment location identified by the host id.
If a host id is provided and the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host, the `execute` statement SHALL end with a test case error.
The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL NOT resolve to `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
If the corresponding formal parameter is not of template kind, an actual parameter (TemplateInstance) of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to an expression.
The `execute` statement SHALL NOT be called from within a test behaviour called from a test case; a test case SHALL only be executed from control behaviour.
The HostId parameter of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a `charstring` value.
The execution of a TTCN-3 test suite IS controlled by the module control function.
The module control function defines the order, sequence, loops, preconditions and actual parameters with which test cases are executed.
The module control function IS an entry point for the execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.
If the module control function has formal parameters, actual values SHALL be provided for them when the module control function is executed.
When the module control function is started, the test system creates a test component called control component.
The control component contains the variables, constants, templates and timers used to control the execution of the test suite.
The control component IS of the component type specified in the `runs on` clause of the module control function.
If the module control function has no `runs on` clause, an empty control component IS created.
Program statements in the module control function CAN specify the order in which test cases are executed and the number of times a test case runs.
If no program statements are used, test cases ARE executed by default in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.
A TTCN-3 tool MAY override the default test case execution order to let a user or tool select a different execution order.
A timer operation MAY be used explicitly in the module control function to control test case execution.
Selection and deselection of test cases CAN be used to control the execution of test cases.
A boolean expression MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
A function returning a `boolean` value MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
Test cases MAY be executed as a group by collecting their `execute` statements in a function that is invoked from the module control function.
The module control function CAN make the order of test case execution depend on the `verdicttype` value returned by a test case.
A `verdicttype` value returned by an `execute` statement MAY be used to select test cases for execution.

An attribute IS a means to give a special characterization or meaning, such as a specific presentation format, a specific encoding, an encoding variant or a user-defined property, to a TTCN-3 language element.
An attribute MAY be associated with a TTCN-3 language element by means of the `with` statement.

A `with` statement MAY be applied to a module, to a global module definition, and to a local definition in the module control function, in a test case, in a function, in an altstep, in a statement block or in a component type definition.
A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to a single language element.
A `with` statement MAY associate attributes, recursively, to fields or elements of a structured type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to members of a component type or a port type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
A `with` statement associated with a single structured type definition MAY associate attributes to several fields of that type by listing the fields in the attribute statement.
A `with` statement associated with a surrounding scope unit or a group MAY associate attributes to all language elements of that scope unit or group.
A `with` statement MAY follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations, and any local definition in component types and in statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.
An attribute MAY be attached to a synonym type.
If a synonym type is a structured type, the attributes in the `with` statement of the synonym type MAY reference fields or elements of that structured type.
An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a general attribute definition of a higher scope.
An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.
An attribute inherited from a type reference IS overriding a general attribute of a higher scope unit that contains the type reference.
A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override the outer `with` statement.
A `with` statement associated with a group nested inside another group SHALL override the `with` statement of the enclosing group.
If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of the attributes of that kind, unless specified otherwise.
An attribute defined for a synonym type IS NOT overriding an existing attribute of a field or element of the synonym type.
An attribute of a synonym type IS applied to a field or element of the synonym type only if the field or element has no valid attribute.
An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS overriding attributes from a higher scope.
An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS valid for the associated language element only.
An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS NOT affecting definitions inside the associated language element, because it is transparent to lower scopes.
An attribute from a higher scope IS affecting the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to a scope between them.
An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS valid.
An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS NOT affecting the definitions inside the module or group.
An attribute definition in a lower scope, or an attribute inherited from a referenced type, MAY be overwritten from a higher scope by using the `override` directive.
The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
If the `override` directive is applied to a type reference, the `override` directive IS NOT affecting the attributes of the original referenced type.
An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type IS overriding the corresponding attribute of the structured type for the identified field or element.

An attribute with the `override` directive applied to a synonym type IS overriding the attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type, unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.
A variant attribute IS always related to an encode attribute.
A variant attribute MAY change without changing the related encode attribute.
An encode attribute SHALL NOT change without overwriting all current variant attributes.
The core language standard IS defining the default overwriting rules for variant attributes.
An extension package of TTCN-3, for example a language mapping, MAY define its own overwriting rules for variant attributes.
A variant attribute IS overwriting a current variant attribute according to the overwriting rules defined in clause 27.1.2.
An encode attribute that overwrites a current encode attribute according to the rules of clause 27.1.2 IS also overwriting the corresponding current variant attribute.
When an encode attribute overwrites a current encode attribute and no new variant attribute is provided, the corresponding current variant attribute IS inactive.
An encode attribute that changes a current encode attribute of an imported language element according to the rules of clause 27.1.3 IS also changing the corresponding current variant attribute.
When an encode attribute changes the current encode attribute of an imported language element and no new variant attribute is provided, the corresponding current variant attribute IS inactive.
An encode attribute of a higher scope that is explicitly listed again in the lower scope and is not overwritten IS retaining all variant attributes related to it.
A variant attribute related to an encoding IS overwriting only the variant attributes related to the same encoding.
An imported language element IS imported together with its attributes.
The attributes of an imported language element MAY be changed by a `with` statement attached to the `import` statement.
When resolving attributes, the `import` statement IS acting as an additional higher scope unit on top of the imported module.
An attribute set in the `import` statement IS valid only within the importing module.
An `import` statement IS located inside an importing module and possibly inside a group.
The attributes of the importing module and of an enclosing group of an `import` statement ARE applying to the imported module too.
If a `with` statement is added to an import of a definition that has its own `with` statement, the attributes of that definition ARE overwriting the attributes added to the `import` statement.
To change the attributes of an imported definition that has its own `with` statement via the `import` statement, the `override` directive SHALL be used.
The `with` statement IS used to associate attributes to TTCN-3 language elements and to sets of language elements.

The `with` statement has the syntax `with "{" { ( encode | variant | display | extension | optional ) [ override | @local ] [ "(" DefinitionRef | FieldReference | AllRef ")" ] [ ( FreeText | ( "{" FreeText { "," FreeText } "}" ) ) "." ] FreeText [ ";" ] } "}"`.
There ARE five kinds of attributes that can be associated with a language element: display, encode, variant, extension and optional.
The `display` attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
The `encode` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
The `variant` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding variants.
The `extension` attribute IS allowing the specification of user-defined attributes.
The `optional` attribute IS allowing the implicit setting of optional fields of records and sets to `omit`.
The argument of an attribute in a `with` statement (the actual attribute) IS a free text string.
A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement IS identifying a definition or field, respectively, within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
An AllRef MAY be used to apply attributes to multiple language elements defined within the scope to which the `with` statement is associated.
An AllRef IS selecting all language elements, or all language elements of a certain kind, defined in a given scope.
An individual language element that is not affected by an attribute MAY be excluded from a set of language elements selected by an AllRef by means of the except clause.

A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement SHALL refer to a definition or field, respectively, which is within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed in a `with` statement, all of them SHALL be without an additional modifier (`override`, `@local`) or all of them SHALL have the same modifier.
Dot notation in the FreeText part of an attribute SHALL NOT be used in attributes other than variant attributes.
A display attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
The display attribute IS introduced by the keyword `display`.
Every TTCN-3 language element MAY have display attributes that specify how the language element is displayed, e.g. in a tabular format.
Special attribute strings related to the display attributes for the graphical presentation format ARE defined in ETSI ES 201 873-3.
A user MAY define other display attributes.
Because user-defined attributes are not standardized, the interpretation of a user-defined attribute MAY differ between tools or MAY not be supported.
At most one display attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or each language element to which a `with` statement is associated.
General or particular encoding rules MAY be specified by using encode and variant attributes.
An encode attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
The encode attribute IS introduced by the keyword `encode`.
An encoding rule IS defining how a value, template, etc. is encoded and transmitted over a communication port and how received signals are decoded.
The TTCN-3 language IS NOT having a default encoding mechanism.
Encoding rules and encoding directives ARE defined in some manner external to TTCN-3.
The encode attribute IS associating a referenced encoding rule or encoding directive with a TTCN-3 definition.
The manner in which the actual encoding rules are defined (e.g. prose, functions) IS outside the scope of the core language standard.
If no specific encoding rules are referenced, the encoding SHALL be a matter for the individual implementation.
Encoding attributes ARE in most cases used in a hierarchical manner.
In the encoding hierarchy the top level IS the entire module, the next level IS a group and the lowest level IS an individual type or definition.
An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying to all types defined in the module, including the built-in TTCN-3 types.
An encode attribute associated with a group IS applying to the user-defined type definitions of the group.
An encode attribute associated with a type or definition IS applying to that single user-defined type or definition.
An encode attribute associated with a field IS applying to that field of a record type, set type or template.
A `with` statement MAY contain more than one encode attribute.
If a `with` statement contains more than one encode attribute, multiple encodings ARE supported in the context where the attribute is used.
The encoding used in encoding and decoding operations MAY be selected dynamically by the `setencode` operation, by a parameter of the predefined codec functions, or inside the codec implementation.
General or particular encoding rules CAN be specified by `encode` and `variant` attributes.
A `variant` attribute IS a reference to a specific encoding variant.
A variant attribute IS denoted by the keyword `variant` in a with statement.
A `variant` attribute SHALL be used to specify a refinement of the currently specified encoding scheme instead of its replacement.
A `variant` attribute IS closely related to `encode` attributes and therefore differs from other attributes.
Additional overwriting rules defined in clause 27.1.2.1 apply to `variant` attributes.
The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for simple basic types IS given in list items a) to e) of clause 27.5 ("8 bit" ... "IEEE754 extended double").

When the variant attribute "8 bit" or "unsigned 8 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 8 bits (single byte) within the system.

When the variant attribute "16 bit" or "unsigned 16 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 16 bits (two bytes) within the system.

When the variant attribute "32 bit" or "unsigned 32 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 32 bits (four bytes) within the system.

When the variant attribute "64 bit" or "unsigned 64 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 64 bits (eight bytes) within the system.

When the variant attribute "IEEE754 float", "IEEE754 double", "IEEE754 extended float" or "IEEE754 extended double" is applied to a float type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to IEEE 754.
The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for charstring and universal charstring types IS given in list items a) to h) following this sentence ("UTF-8" ... "8 bit").

When the variant attribute "UTF-8" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-8 as defined in clause 10.1 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-16" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16 as defined in clause 10.4 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16LE as defined in clause 10.3 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-16BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16BE as defined in clause 10.2 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-32" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32 as defined in clause 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-32LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32LE as defined in clause 10.6 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "UTF-32BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32BE as defined in clause 10.5 of ISO/IEC 10646.

When the variant attribute "8 bit" is applied to a charstring or universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the 8-bit coded representation specified in ISO/IEC 10646.
A UCS encoding scheme permits an optional signature (byte order mark, BOM) to be present in encoded character strings.
A UCS encoding scheme variant attribute IS NOT specifying whether signatures (BOM) are present in the encoded value; the presence of signatures is an option of the encoder.
A decoder SHOULD be able to process signatures (BOM) in the decoding process.
The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for structured types IS given in list item a) following this sentence ("IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6").
When the variant attribute "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" is applied to a record type, the value SHALL be handled as an IDL fixed point decimal value.
A predefined variant attribute MAY be used in combination with a more general encode attribute specified at a higher level.

When a universal charstring has the variant attribute "UTF-8" within a module that has the global encode attribute "BER:1997", each character of the string value IS first encoded following the UTF-8 rules and the resulting UTF-8 value IS then encoded following the BER rules.
An invalid encoding rule SHALL be specified in a referenceable source external to the module in the same way as valid encoding rules are referenced.
If multiple encodings are used, the value of a variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.
A variant attribute whose value is composed of an encoding reference and a variant value separated by a dot IS called an encoding related variant attribute.
The first part (before the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS the specification of the encodings the variant is related to.
When the variant is related to a single encode attribute, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string.
When the variant is related to multiple encodings, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets.
The second part (following the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string that specifies the variant value.
An encoding related variant attribute IS valid only when the related encoding is selected.
If multiple encodings are used, a variant attribute SHALL NOT be defined without an encoding reference.
A with statement MAY contain any number of variant attributes.
When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot SHALL resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.
An extension attribute CAN be used for proprietary extensions to TTCN-3.
A with statement MAY contain any number of extension attributes.
An extension attribute IS denoted by the keyword `extension` in a with statement.
An extension attribute MAY be specified by the user for any TTCN-3 language element.
The interpretation of a user-defined (extension) attribute IS not standardized and may differ between tools of different vendors or not be supported at all.
An optional attribute IS used to indicate that the optional fields of constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables of record and set types are implicitly set to `omit`.
An optional attribute IS denoted by the keyword `optional` in a with statement.
An optional attribute MAY be associated with a constant, module parameter, template, variable or template variable.
An optional attribute MAY be associated with a module, group, function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition.

When an optional attribute is associated with a function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition, it SHALL have effect on all constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within that definition.
When an optional attribute is associated with a function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition, it SHALL NOT have effect on the enframing definition itself.

When no value of the optional attribute is specified for a definition, either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope, the optional attribute of that definition IS implicitly "explicit omit".
The predefined (standardized) optional attribute values IS one of "implicit omit" and "explicit omit".
With the optional attribute "implicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS set to `omit`.
The "implicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.
With the optional attribute "explicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS left undefined.
The "explicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.

For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each assignment in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.

For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each usage of it as an `out` or `inout` actual parameter in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.
Assigning the "implicit omit" attribute to a variable CAN have a negative runtime performance impact.
A TTCN-3 tool SHOULD identify and optimize cases where the implicit omit operations are not needed, e.g. where it can be decided statically that no optional field could have become undefined.
An optional attribute SHALL NOT be associated directly with a data type definition, port type definition, procedure signature definition or import statement.

When an optional attribute is associated with a module, group, function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type, it SHALL NOT have any effect on the data type, port type, procedure signature or import statement definitions contained in it.
At most one optional attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.
TTCN-3 provides operations for retrieving the attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.
An attribute retrieval operation has the syntax ( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( `display` | `encode` | `variant` | `extension` | `optional` ) [ "(" Expression ")" ].
An attribute retrieval operation returns the actual value of the attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter preceding the dot.
The variable or template preceding the dot of an attribute retrieval operation MAY be uninitialized.
The attribute kind retrieved by an attribute retrieval operation IS denoted by the keyword (`display`, `encode`, `variant`, `extension` or `optional`) following the dot.
An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can be present only once (`display`, `optional`) returns a value of universal charstring type.
If a `display` or `optional` attribute is not defined, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty string.
An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can occur multiple times (`encode`, `variant`, `extension`) returns a value of a record of universal charstring type.
If an `encode`, `variant` or `extension` attribute is not present, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty record of value.
An attribute retrieval operation for a `variant` attribute MAY be followed by an optional parameter.
If no parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns only the variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.
If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns the variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.
The optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be used only for retrieving `variant` attributes.
The Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be of universal charstring type.
An error SHALL be produced if the Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation is not one of the valid encode attributes of the referenced type or template.
The `setencode` operation CAN be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select, for the affected ports, a single encode attribute value for a type that has multiple encode attributes.
The `setencode` operation has the syntax ( SingleExpression | `all port` | `self` ) "." `setencode` "(" Type "," SingleExpression ")".
The `setencode` operation dynamically restricts the encode attribute values of the referenced type, or of its fields or elements, to a single value.
When the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port reference, the encoding configuration IS valid for all sending and receiving operations of that port.
When the `setencode` operation is applied with `all port`, the encoding configuration IS valid for the sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component.
When the `setencode` operation is applied with `self`, the encoding configuration IS valid for all codec functions and communication operations of the current component.

If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression of the `setencode` operation equals one of them, the `setencode` operation reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.
The `setencode` reduction procedure IS applied recursively to all elements and fields of the referenced type.
After the `setencode` operation is executed, all other encode attributes of the referenced type and the variants related to them IS dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.
A repeated call of the `setencode` operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.
Previous calls of the `setencode` operation referencing the same type IS NOT considered by a repeated call.
The encoding of a type CAN be changed during test execution by repeated `setencode` calls using different encodings.
The `setencode` operation MAY reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference.
A `setencode` operation with an extended type reference IS useful for payload fields of container protocols and allows dynamic configuration of the proper encoding for payload fields.

If an extended type reference was used in a `setencode` operation, subsequent `setencode` calls for the whole type or any element containing the referenced field SHALL NOT change the encoding dynamically configured for that field or element and its sub-fields.

If the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in or out type list of the related port type, or be a reference to a field or element, on any level of nesting, of such a type.
The SingleExpression in the second parameter of the `setencode` operation SHALL be compatible with the universal charstring type.
If present, the SingleExpression preceding the `setencode` keyword SHALL be of a port type.
The syntax of TTCN-3 IS defined in annex A using extended BNF (called BNF).
The syntactic metanotation of table A.1 IS parsed from left to right.
The metanotation operators HAVE the precedence, from highest to lowest: repetition and optional, grouping, concatenation, alternative, definition.
A TTCN-3 language construct (definition, declaration, statement or operation) SHALL be terminated with a semi-colon (`;`), except where clause A.1.2 makes the semi-colon optional.
If a language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (`}`), the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
If the symbol following a language construct is a right-hand curly brace (`}`), i.e. the construct is the last statement in a statement block, the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
A comma-separated list IS terminated by a right parenthesis (`)`), a right-hand curly brace (`}`), a left-hand curly brace (`{`) or a semi-colon (`;`).

A comma-separated list with a variable number of items MAY have a trailing comma immediately before its closing right parenthesis (`)`) or right-hand curly brace (`}`), or before the next lexical symbol `{` or `;`.
A TTCN-3 identifier IS case sensitive.
An identifier SHALL only contain lowercase letters (a-z), uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore (`_`) symbol.
An identifier SHALL begin with a letter and SHALL NOT begin with a numeric digit or an underscore.
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `abc xyz` denotes abc followed by xyz (concatenation).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `|` denotes alternative.
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `[abc]` denotes 0 or 1 instances of abc (optional).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `{abc}` denotes 0 or more instances of abc (repetition 1).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `{abc}+` denotes 1 or more instances of abc (repetition 2).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `{abc}#(n, m)` denotes n to m instances of abc (repetition 3).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `(...)` denotes textual grouping (grouping).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `Abc` denotes the non-terminal symbol abc (non-terminal).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `"abc"` denotes a terminal symbol abc (terminal).
In the syntactic metanotation (table A.1), the notation `::=` denotes is defined to be (definition of a non-terminal).
A free-text comment MAY appear anywhere in a TTCN-3 specification.
A comment MAY contain any graphical character defined in ISO/IEC 10646.
A block comment SHALL be opened by the symbol pair `/*`.
A block comment SHALL be closed by the symbol pair `*/`.
A block comment SHALL NOT be nested inside another block comment.
A line comment SHALL be opened by the symbol pair `//`.
A line comment SHALL be closed by a newline or by the end of file.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for begin/end list symbols ARE `(` and `)`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for element specifier symbols ARE `[` and `]`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for range symbol IS `..`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for ellipsis IS `...`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for line and block comment symbols ARE `/*`, `*/` and `//`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for statement separator symbol IS `;`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for arithmetic operator symbols ARE `+`, `/`, `-` and `*`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for concatenation operator symbol IS `&`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for relational operator symbols ARE `!=`, `==`, `>=`, `<=`, `<` and `>`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for shift operator symbols ARE `<<` and `>>`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for rotate operator symbols ARE `<@` and `@>`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for string enclosure symbols ARE `"` and `'`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for wildcard/matching symbols ARE `?` and `*`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for assignment symbol IS `:=`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for communication operation assignment symbol IS `->`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for bitstring, hexstring and octetstring value symbols ARE `B`, `H` and `O`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for float exponent symbol IS `E`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for list element separator symbol ARE `,`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for field reference symbol IS `.`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for decoded field reference symbol IS `=>`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for not-implemented identifier symbol IS `???`.
The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for begin/end block symbols ARE `{` and `}`.
A predefined function identifier defined in table 15 and described in annex C SHALL be treated as a reserved word.
A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL NOT be used as an identifier in a TTCN-3 module.
A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
A special TTCN-3 terminal (modifier) IS an @-symbol directly followed by an identifier.
A special TTCN-3 terminal consisting of an @-symbol followed by an identifier SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
The identifier part of a modifier terminal CAN be used in combination with the @-symbol, which gives the annotated language element a specific semantics.
The identifier part of a modifier terminal (e.g. `lazy`, `fuzzy`, `nocase`) CAN also be used as an ordinary identifier without special meaning.

The TTCN-3 reserved words (table A.3) ARE: action, activate, address, alive, all, alt, altstep, and, and4b, any, anytype, bitstring, boolean, break, case, call, catch, char, charstring, check, clear, complement, component, connect, const, continue, control, create, deactivate, decmatch, default, disconnect, display, do, done, else, encode, enumerated, error, except, exception, execute, extends, extension, external, fail, false, float, for, friend, from, function, getverdict, getcall, getreply, goto, group, halt, hexstring, if, ifpresent, import, in, inconc, infinity, inout, integer, interleave, isbound, ischosen, ispresent, isvalue, kill, killed, label, language, length, log, map, match, message, mixed, mod, modifies, module, modulepar, mtc, noblock, none, not, not_a_number, not4b, nowait, null, octetstring, of, omit, on, optional, or, or4b, out, override, param, pass, pattern, permutation, port, present, private, procedure, public, raise, read, receive, record, recursive, rem, repeat, reply, return, running, runs, select, self, send, sender, set, setencode, setverdict, signature, start, stop, subset, superset, system, template, testcase, timeout, timer, to, trigger, true, type, union, universal, unmap, value, valueof, var, variant, verdicttype, while, with, xor, xor4b.
A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 IS used as a keyword inside the TTCN-3 extension packages.
A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 (extension package reserved word) SHALL NOT be used as an identifier in a TTCN-3 module.
A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 (extension package reserved word) SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.

Elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) SHALL be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2, according to the TTCN-3 syntax.
Whitespace MAY consist of one or more of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters HT (9), LF (10), VT (11), FF (12), CR (13) and SP (32) in any combination.
Each of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters LF (10), VT (11), FF (12) and CR (13) IS a newline (end of line).
A CR (13) character directly followed by an LF (10) character IS a single end of line (e.g. the sequence CR LF CR LF VT denotes 3 lines).
A character or character sequence that is a valid newline IS also valid whitespace.
The TTCN-3 terminals which are modifiers (table A.4) ARE: `@abstract`, `@control`, `@decoded`, `@default`, `@deterministic`, `@fuzzy`, `@index`, `@lazy`, `@local`, `@nocase` and `@nodefault`.

The TTCN-3 terminals which are reserved words in extension packages (table A.5) ARE: `apply`, `assert`, `at`, `configuration`, `conjunct`, `cont`, `delta`, `disjunct`, `duration`, `finished`, `history`, `implies`, `inv`, `mode`, `notinv`, `now`, `object`, `onentry`, `onexit`, `par`, `prev`, `realtime`, `seq`, `setstate`, `static`, `stepsize`, `stream`, `timestamp`, `until`, `values`, `wait`.
Only the CR and LF control characters SHOULD be used for newline, because VT and FF may cause problems with some conventional text editors.
Only the HT, LF, CR and SP control characters SHOULD be used for whitespace, because VT and FF may cause problems with some conventional text editors.
At most one UnionFieldDef of a UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef SHALL contain a DefaultModifier (`@default`).
The SingleExpression of an IntegerValueOrRange in an Enumeration SHALL evaluate to a statically bound integer value.
The AllowedValuesSpec of a SubTypeSpec SHALL be of the same type as the type or field being subtyped.
The RangeDef production in a TemplateOrRange SHALL only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types.
When a charstring or universal charstring type is subtyped, a range and values SHALL NOT be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec.
The StringLength production SHALL only be used with string types or to limit the length of record of and set of types.
Each SingleExpression bound of a StringLength SHALL evaluate to a non-negative integer value, and the upper bound MAY additionally be `infinity`.
A FormalValuePar in a TemplateOrValueFormalPar (template formal parameter list) SHALL resolve to an `in` parameter.
Within a BaseTemplateBody, the ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
The ExtendedIdentifier of a SingleTemplateExpression that is followed by an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL refer to an enumerated value with an associated value.
Each BaseTemplateBody in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be an integer template.
The limits of each Range in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be integer values.
The PredefinedType and TypeReference alternatives of a StructFieldRef SHALL be used only for anytype value notation.
The PredefinedType alternative of a StructFieldRef SHALL NOT be the `anytype` keyword.
The Identifier in a ParRef SHALL be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition.
An IndexRef MAY be used for array types and for record of, set of and map types.
The IndexRef notation MAY be used for a string element reference inside a charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring or hexstring value.
The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL resolve to a value of integer type.
A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL be used only when the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL NOT be used when the MatchingSymbol is not used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.

When a MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch alternatives SHALL NOT be used.

The characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^" and "N" ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.

The characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q" and "," ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.
The SingleExpression of a WildcardLengthMatch SHALL evaluate to type integer.
A Bound SHALL evaluate to type integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.
If a Bound evaluates to type charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be 1.
`infinity` as a lower Bound and `-infinity` as an upper Bound SHALL be used only for float types.
If an ActualParAssignment assigns to a formal value parameter, the in-line template (TemplateInstance) SHALL evaluate to a value.
When the corresponding formal parameter is not a template formal parameter, the TemplateInstance of an ActualPar SHALL resolve to one or more SingleExpressions.
The parenthesized ActualParList part of a FunctionInstance SHALL be present unless the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced module control function has no formal parameters.
The Identifier of a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be one of the predefined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C.
A CaseInsenModifier in a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be present only if the Identifier is "regexp".
If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a DoneStatement (`done` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a KilledStatement (`killed` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL be type compatible with the return type of the signature.
The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.
The FieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a ParRef.
The ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a type definition identifier.
Each array bound (SingleExpression) of an ArrayDef SHALL resolve to a non-negative value of integer type.
The ReferencedEnumValue alternative of a ReferencedValue SHALL be used only for referencing enumerated values.
A ReferencedValue that does not reference an enumerated value SHALL use the ExtendedIdentifier [ExtendedFieldReference] alternative.
The ExtendedEnumReference of a ReferencedEnumValue SHALL be present if and only if the Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list.
A Char in a charstring IS a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.
A Char in a universal charstring IS a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.

An ExtendedAlphaNum IS a graphical character from the BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets of ISO/IEC 10646, i.e. a character from char(0,0,0,32) to char(0,0,0,126), from char(0,0,0,161) to char(0,0,0,172) or from char(0,0,0,174) to char(0,0,0,255).
An NLChar IS any sequence of the newline characters LF(10), VT(11), FF(12) and CR(13) of ITU-T T.50 that constitutes a newline.
An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference refers to a type definition if the type of the referenced definition in which the ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference is used is anytype.
An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
The square brackets with dash "[-]" SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing the inner type of a record of, set of or array type.
In a function returning a value, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type.

In a function returning a template, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type.
Within a CompoundExpression, the ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types.
A BooleanExpression SHALL resolve to a value of type boolean.
Within a CompoundConstExpression, the ArrayConstExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
When the left hand side of an Assignment is a value variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side.

When the left hand side of an Assignment is a template variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side.
If a SingleExpression contains more than one XorExpression, the XorExpressions (operands of `or`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If a XorExpression contains more than one AndExpression, the AndExpressions (operands of `xor`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If a AndExpression contains more than one NotExpression, the NotExpressions (operands of `and`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
The operand of the `not` operator in a NotExpression SHALL be of type boolean or a type derived from boolean.
If an EqualExpression contains more than one RelExpression, the RelExpressions SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If an EqualExpression contains only one RelExpression, that RelExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
If a RelExpression contains both ShiftExpressions, each ShiftExpression SHALL evaluate to a specific integer, enumerated or float value or a value of a type derived from these types.
Each BitOrExpression operand of a ShiftExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
If a ShiftExpression contains more than one operand, the right-hand operand SHALL be of type integer or a type derived from integer.
If the shift operator is `<<` or `>>`, the left-hand operand SHALL resolve to bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or a type derived from these types.
If a BitOrExpression contains more than one BitXorExpression, the BitXorExpressions (operands of `or4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If a BitXorExpression contains more than one BitAndExpression, the BitAndExpressions (operands of `xor4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If a BitAndExpression contains more than one BitNotExpression, the BitNotExpressions (operands of `and4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
If the `not4b` operator is present in a BitNotExpression, its operand SHALL be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or a type derived from these types.
Each MulExpression of an AddExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp resolves to StringOp, the MulExpressions SHALL be valid operands for StringOp.
If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp, both MulExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
If an AddExpression contains only one MulExpression, that MulExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
Each UnaryExpression of a MulExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
If a MulExpression contains more than one UnaryExpression, the UnaryExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
If a UnaryExpression contains a UnaryOp, its Primary SHALL resolve to a specific value of type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldReference refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.
An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear on the left-hand side of an assignment.
A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear in a type reference.
The Identifier of a DecodedFieldType SHALL resolve to a type.
The operands of the binary `+` and `-` operators (AddOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
The operands of the `*`, `/`, `rem` and `mod` operators (MultiplyOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
The operand of the unary `+` and `-` operators (UnaryOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).

The operands of the concatenation operator `&` (StringOp) SHALL be of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of or array types, or types derived from these types.
If the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct, each TemplateInstance of a SelectCase SHALL be an Identifier.
A matching mechanism specified in annex B MAY be used in a template.
A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be used outside of a template.
A specific value IS the basic matching mechanism of TTCN-3 templates.
A specific value in a template IS an expression that does not contain any matching mechanism or wildcard.
