If the referenced template of `substr` is of a binary string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a specific value containing as many AnyElement symbols as the count parameter.
If the referenced binary string template of `substr` contains AnyValueOrNone, the `ifpresent` matching attribute SHALL be added to the returned value.

If the referenced template of `substr` is of a character string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a pattern containing as many ? metacharacters as the count parameter.
If the referenced character string template of `substr` contains AnyValueOrNone, the `ifpresent` matching attribute SHALL be added to the returned pattern.
If inpar of `substr` contains a length matching attribute, the value returned by `substr` SHALL NOT contain that length matching attribute.
If inpar of `substr` contains the `ifpresent` matching attribute, the value returned by `substr` SHALL also contain the `ifpresent` matching attribute.

If inpar of `substr` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `substr` SHALL have the present restriction.
If inpar of `substr` contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the value returned by `substr` SHALL have the value restriction.

When inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or an array, it SHALL contain only specific values, AnyElement or combined templates whose elements are specific values, AnyElement or combined templates.
When inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or an array, the substring or subsequence to be returned SHALL NOT contain AnyElement or a combined template.
The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `substr` in addition to the error causes specific to `substr`.
If the index actual parameter of `substr` is less than zero, an error SHALL occur.
If the count actual parameter of `substr` is less than zero, an error SHALL occur.
If inpar of `substr` contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + count is greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
If inpar of `substr` is a template of a character or binary string type containing a matching mechanism other than those allowed for indexing in clause 15.6.1, an error SHALL occur.

If inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or array containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or combined template, or a combined template whose elements are matching mechanisms other than specific values, AnyElement or combined templates, an error SHALL occur.
If the template passed to inpar of `substr` is not of type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of`, `set of` or array, an error SHALL occur.
The `replace` predefined function has the syntax replace(in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer len, in template (present) any repl) return any_string_or_sequence type.
The `replace` function SHALL replace the substring or subsequence of inpar starting at index index with length len by repl and return the resulting string or sequence.
The `replace` function SHALL NOT modify the inpar actual parameter.
If len is 0, the `replace` function SHALL insert repl into inpar at position index.
If index is 0, the `replace` function SHALL insert repl at the beginning of inpar.
If index equals lengthof(inpar), the `replace` function SHALL insert repl at the end of inpar.
If the inpar actual parameter of `replace` is a literal whose type is not explicitly given, the type of inpar SHALL be retrieved from the value contents.
The inpar and repl actual parameters of `replace` and the returned string or sequence SHALL be of the same root type.
The `replace` function MAY be applied to `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, any character string, `record of`, `set of` and array values.
Indexing in strings for `replace` starts from zero.
If inpar or repl or both of `replace` are an array, the returned type IS `record of`, because the root type of an array is `record of`.
When inpar or repl of `replace` is an array, the indexing in inpar and/or repl and in the returned value CAN differ.
The inpar actual parameter of `replace` MAY contain a template.
A template passed as inpar of `replace` SHALL fulfil the requirements on the inpar parameter of the `substr` function specified in clause C.4.2.
The repl actual parameter of `replace` MAY contain a template.
A template passed as repl of `replace` SHALL contain only a specific value, a pattern or AnyValue, without any matching attributes attached to it.
If either inpar or repl of `replace` contains a template, the `replace` function SHALL return a template with the present restriction according to the rules of clause C.4.3.
If both inpar and repl of `replace` contain AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `? length (index..infinity)`.
If inpar of `replace` contains AnyValueOrNone and repl contains AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `* length (index..infinity)`.

In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a binary string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone.
In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a character string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to pattern "*".
The AnyValue-to-AnyElementOrNone conversion of repl in `replace` SHALL produce a binary string compatible with the type of inpar.
When inpar of `replace` is of a character string type, the converted repl SHALL be pattern "*".

When inpar or repl is a template and neither of the AnyValue rules applies, `replace` SHALL return a value equal to substr(inpar, 0, index) & repl & substr(inpar, index + len, lengthof(inpar) - index - len).

If any `substr` call of the `replace` concatenation formula yields a template with the `ifpresent` matching attribute, the attribute SHALL be removed before concatenation and added to the final result of the concatenation.

If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the present restriction.
If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the value restriction.
The template returned by the `replace` concatenation formula IS without any length matching attribute, because `substr` removes length matching attributes.
The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `replace` in addition to the error causes specific to `replace`.
If inpar or repl of `replace` is not of a string, `record of`, `set of` or array type, an error SHALL occur.
If inpar and repl of `replace` are of different root types, an error SHALL occur.
If the index actual parameter of `replace` is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
If the len actual parameter of `replace` is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
If inpar of `replace` contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + len is greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.

The `encvalue` predefined function has the signature encvalue(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return bitstring.
The `encvalue` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into a bitstring.
When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue` IS subject to the same restrictions as the argument of the `send` operation.
The bitstring returned by `encvalue` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
The test system NEED NOT check the correctness of the bitstring returned by `encvalue`.
The optional `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue` IS used for passing additional encoding information to the codec.
If the `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue` is omitted, no additional encoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
Each general error cause of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to a call of `encvalue`.
A call of `encvalue` SHALL cause an error when encoding fails due to a runtime system problem, i.e. when no encoding function exists for the actual type of `inpar`.

The `decvalue` predefined function has the signature decvalue(inout bitstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
The `decvalue` function IS the predefined function that decodes a bitstring into a value.
The test system SHALL treat the bitstring `encoded_value` passed to `decvalue` as an encoded instance of the actual type of `decoded_value`.
The optional `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue` IS used for passing additional decoding information to the codec.
If the `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue` is omitted, no additional decoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used bits) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
The `decvalue` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
The return value 0 of `decvalue` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
The return value 1 of `decvalue` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue` SHALL return 1.
The return value 2 of `decvalue` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough bits.
Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue`.

The `encvalue_unichar` predefined function has the signature encvalue_unichar(in template (value) any inpar, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return universal charstring.
The `encvalue_unichar` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into a universal charstring.
When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_unichar` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS subject to the same restrictions as the argument of the `send` operation.
The universal charstring returned by `encvalue_unichar` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
The test system NEED NOT check the correctness of the universal charstring returned by `encvalue_unichar`.
If the optional `string_serialization` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" IS used.
The optional `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS used for passing additional encoding information to the codec.
If the `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` is omitted, no additional encoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue_unichar` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue_unichar` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
The `string_serialization` actual parameter of `encvalue_unichar` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
The octet serialization of the characters used by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
When `string_serialization` of `encvalue_unichar` is "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", big-endian ordering SHALL be used.
A call encvalue_unichar(inpar, string_serialization, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding) IS equivalent to oct2unichar(bit2oct(encvalue(inpar, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding)), string_serialization).
The `encvalue_unichar` function IS executed by first invoking `encvalue` to encode the value passed in `inpar` to a bitstring.
The bitstring produced inside `encvalue_unichar` IS converted to an octetstring by `bit2oct`.
The octetstring produced inside `encvalue_unichar` IS converted to a universal charstring by `oct2unichar`.
The `string_serialization` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS the definition of how the encoded octets (the encoded bitstring received from the codec) contain the characters.
The universal charstring produced by `oct2unichar` IS returned as the result of `encvalue_unichar`.
Each general error cause of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to a call of `encvalue_unichar`.
A call of `encvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error when encoding fails due to a runtime system problem, i.e. when no encoding function exists for the actual type of `inpar`.
A call of `encvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error when the given string encoding (`string_serialization`) is not recognized.

The `decvalue_unichar` predefined function has the signature decvalue_unichar(inout universal charstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
The `decvalue_unichar` function IS the predefined function that decodes (part of) a universal charstring into a value.
The test system SHALL treat a prefix of the universal charstring `encoded_value` passed to `decvalue_unichar` as an encoded instance of the actual type of `decoded_value`.
The optional `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS used for passing additional decoding information to the codec.
If the `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` is omitted, no additional decoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue_unichar` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue_unichar` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used characters) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
The `decvalue_unichar` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
The return value 0 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
The return value 1 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue_unichar` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue_unichar` SHALL return 1.
The return value 2 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough characters.
If the optional `string_serialization` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" IS used.
The `string_serialization` actual parameter of `decvalue_unichar` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
The octet serialization of the characters used by `decvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
When `string_serialization` of `decvalue_unichar` is "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", big-endian ordering SHALL be used.

A call of `decvalue_unichar` IS equivalent to converting `encoded_value` with oct2bit(unichar2oct(encoded_value, string_serialization)), calling `decvalue` on the result with `decoded_value`, `decoding_info` and `dynamic_encoding`, and returning the `decvalue` result.
If the inner `decvalue` call of `decvalue_unichar` returns 0, `encoded_value` IS assigned oct2unichar(bit2oct(remaining bitstring), string_serialization).
The `decvalue_unichar` function IS executed by first converting the universal charstring passed in `encoded_value` into an octetstring using `unichar2oct`.
The `string_serialization` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS the control of how the characters are converted into octets (i.e. how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).
The octetstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS converted into a bitstring by `oct2bit`.
The bitstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS passed to the standard `decvalue` function, which performs the actual decoding.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the undecoded part of the message IS converted from bitstring to octetstring by `bit2oct` and then to universal charstring by `oct2unichar`.
If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the universal charstring obtained from the undecoded part IS assigned to the `encoded_value` parameter.
The result of the inner `decvalue` call IS returned to the caller as the result of `decvalue_unichar`.
Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue_unichar`.

The `encvalue_o` predefined function has the signature encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "", out integer bit_length) return octetstring.
The `encvalue_o` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into an octetstring.
When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` IS subject to the same restrictions as the argument of the `send` operation.
The octetstring returned by `encvalue_o` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
The test system NEED NOT check the correctness of the octetstring returned by `encvalue_o`.
If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, the encoded message IS left-aligned in the octetstring returned by `encvalue_o`.

If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, each of the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits of the least significant octet returned by `encvalue_o` IS 0.
The bit length of the encoded message CAN be assigned to a variable through the `out` formal parameter `bit_length` of `encvalue_o`.
The optional `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_o` IS used for passing additional encoding information to the codec.
If the `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_o` is omitted, no additional encoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue_o` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue_o` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue_o` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
Each general error cause of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to a call of `encvalue_o`.
A call of `encvalue_o` SHALL cause an error when encoding fails due to a runtime system problem, i.e. when no encoding function exists for the actual type of `inpar`.

The `decvalue_o` predefined function has the signature decvalue_o(inout octetstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
The `decvalue_o` function IS the predefined function that decodes an octetstring into a value.
The test system SHALL treat the octetstring `encoded_value` passed to `decvalue_o` as an encoded instance of the actual type of `decoded_value`.
The optional `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_o` IS used for passing additional decoding information to the codec.
If the `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_o` is omitted, no additional decoding information IS sent to the codec.
The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue_o` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue_o` call.
The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue_o` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used octets) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
If decoding by `decvalue_o` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
The `decvalue_o` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
The return value 0 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
The return value 1 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue_o` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue_o` SHALL return 1.
The return value 2 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough octets.
Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue_o`.
The `get_stringencoding` predefined function has the signature get_stringencoding(in octetstring encoded_value) return charstring.
The `get_stringencoding` function IS the predefined function that analyses `encoded_value` and returns its UCS encoding scheme according to clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646.
The `get_stringencoding` function SHALL return the identified UCS encoding scheme of `encoded_value` as a charstring.
If the encoding scheme of `encoded_value` cannot be determined unambiguously, `get_stringencoding` SHALL return the charstring "<unknown>".
When present, the initial octet sequence (byte order mark) IS sufficient to identify the encoding scheme unambiguously.
When no byte order mark is present, `get_stringencoding` MAY use other symptoms (e.g. an odd number of octets or the bit distribution of UTF-8) to identify the encoding scheme unambiguously.
The `remove_bom` predefined function has the signature remove_bom(in octetstring encoded_value) return octetstring.
The `remove_bom` function IS the predefined function that removes the optional FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence (byte order mark) from the beginning of `encoded_value`.
If `encoded_value` contains no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence, `remove_bom` SHALL return the value of `encoded_value` unchanged.
The `rnd` function has the signature `rnd([in float seed]) return float`, with an optional `in` formal parameter `seed` of type `float` and a return value of type `float`.
The `rnd` function returns a (pseudo) random `float` value that is greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.
The random number generator used by `rnd` IS initialized separately per test component and per module control function.
The random number generator of `rnd` MAY be initialized by passing an optional seed value of type `float` as actual parameter of `rnd`.
If `rnd` is called without a new seed value, the last random number generated by `rnd` IS used as seed for the next random number.

If the random number generator has not been initialized with a seed value, a seed value calculated from the system time IS used when `rnd` is called for the first time in a test component or in the module control function.
Each time `rnd` is initialized with the same seed value, `rnd` SHALL repeat the same sequence of random numbers.
Each test component and the module control function has its own random seed, to keep parallel testing deterministic.
A separate random seed per test component and module control function allows for better reproducibility of test executions.
The `rnd` function always uses the seed of the test component or module control function that calls it.
A random integer in the range lowerbound..upperbound CAN be produced with the expression `float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound + 1) * rnd()) + lowerbound`.
The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `rnd`.
If the seed actual parameter of `rnd` is `infinity`, `-infinity` or `not_a_number`, an error SHALL occur.
The `testcasename` function has the signature `testcasename() return charstring`, with no formal parameters and a return value of type `charstring`.
The `testcasename` function SHALL return the unqualified name of the currently executing test case, also when called by a parallel test component.
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-8 coding scheme IS EF BB BF.
For UTF-8, the initial octet sequence (BOM) is not required and IS of no effect as a signature.
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16BE coding scheme IS FE FF.
For UTF-16BE, the octet sequence FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16LE coding scheme IS FF FE.
For UTF-16LE, the octet sequence FF FE IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16 coding scheme IS FE FF or FF FE.
For UTF-16, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32BE coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF.
For UTF-32BE, the octet sequence 00 00 FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32LE coding scheme IS FF FE 00 00.
For UTF-32LE, the octet sequence FF FE 00 00 IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32 coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF or FF FE 00 00.
For UTF-32, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and 00 00 FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
When `testcasename` is called while the module control function is executing and no test case is executing, `testcasename` SHALL return the empty string.
The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `testcasename`.

The `hostid` function has the signature `hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring`, with an `in` formal parameter `idkind` of type `charstring` and a return value of type `charstring`.
If `hostid` is called without an actual parameter, the `idkind` formal parameter IS "Ipv4orIPv6" by default.
The `hostid` function SHALL return, as a `charstring`, the host id of the test component or module control function executing the `hostid` function.
The `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` specifies the expected format of the returned host id.
The predefined values of the `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` ARE "Ipv4orIPv6", "Ipv4" and "Ipv6".
If `idkind` is "Ipv4orIPv6" and an Ipv4 address is available, the string returned by `hostid` IS an Ipv4 address.
If `idkind` is "Ipv4orIPv6" and no Ipv4 address but an Ipv6 address is available, the string returned by `hostid` IS a character string representation of the Ipv6 address.
If `idkind` is "Ipv4", the string returned by `hostid` SHALL be an Ipv4 address.
If `idkind` is "Ipv6", the string returned by `hostid` SHALL be an Ipv6 address.
If `hostid` cannot retrieve any host id, `hostid` SHALL return the empty string.
If `hostid` can retrieve only a host id of a kind different from the kind given by the `idkind` actual parameter, `hostid` SHALL return the empty string.
The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `hostid`.
A preprocessing macro IS a macro that a preprocessor or compiler replaces with a charstring or integer value before compilation.
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring value.
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template (e.g. a pattern string).
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a TTCN-3 comment.
A preprocessing macro MAY be used in TTCN-3 code wherever a charstring or integer value, respectively, can be used.
The `__MODULE__` preprocessing macro denotes the name of the module in which the macro is used.
A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__MODULE__` with the actual module name as a charstring value.
The `__FILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, of the file in which the macro is used.
A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__FILE__` with the actual canonical (absolute) file name as a charstring value.
The format of the canonical file name IS NOT specified by the standard and depends on the operating system.
The `__BFILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, of the file in which the macro is used.
A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__BFILE__` with the actual basic (relative) file name as a charstring value.
The format of the basic file name IS NOT specified by the standard and depends on the operating system.
The `__LINE__` preprocessing macro denotes the line number, in the file, of the line in which the macro is used.
A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace each occurrence of `__LINE__` with the actual line number as an integer value.
The first line of a file IS line number 1.
Each newline SHALL increase the line number by 1.
A newline inside a commented line SHALL also increase the line number by 1.
The `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro denotes the unqualified name of the lowest named basic scope unit in which the macro is used.

The basic scope units of TTCN-3 ARE the module definitions part, the module control function, component types, functions, altsteps, testcases, statement blocks, templates and user-defined named types.
A statement block IS NOT named.
A `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro used in a statement block refers to the next higher named basic scope unit.
A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__SCOPE__` with a charstring value determined by the kind of the lowest named scope unit.
If the lowest named scope unit is the module definitions part, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the module name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is the module control function, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the charstring value "control".
If the lowest named scope unit is a component type definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the component type name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is a testcase definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the testcase name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is an altstep definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the altstep name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is a function definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the function name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is a local or global template definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the template name as a charstring value.
If the lowest named scope unit is a user-defined named type definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the type name as a charstring value.
The `__SCOPE__` preprocessing macro CANNOT retrieve the names of other kinds of definitions, such as groups or global constants.
